name: shadcn/ui
description: A collection of reusable components built with Radix UI and Tailwind CSS. Components are copied into your project, not installed as a dependency.

color-primitives.description: Raw color palette values. These are the base colors from which semantic tokens are derived.

color.description: Semantic color tokens. Values shown are the default light theme.

primary.description: Primary brand color used for prominent interactive elements and emphasis.

secondary.description: Secondary color for less prominent interactive elements.

muted.description: Muted background color for subtle UI areas.

muted-foreground.description: Text color for de-emphasized or secondary text.

accent.description: Accent color for highlights and hover states.

destructive.description: Color for destructive actions such as delete or remove.

ring.description: Focus ring color for interactive elements.

popover.description: Surface color for floating panels (Popover, DropdownMenu, Tooltip content).

popover-foreground.description: Text color on floating panel surfaces.

spacing.description: Spacing scale based on a 4px (0.25rem) base unit at the default root font size.

sp-1.description: 4px. Smallest spacing unit, used for tight internal padding.

sp-2.description: 8px. Small spacing, used for gaps between related elements.

sp-4.description: 16px. Standard spacing for padding and margins.

sp-8.description: 32px. Large spacing for major section separation.

radius-sm.description: Smaller border radius for nested or compact elements.

radius-lg.description: Larger border radius for prominent containers.

button.name: Button
button.description: An interactive element that triggers an action when activated. Built on a native button element with support for Radix UI Slot composition via asChild.
button.whenToUse: Use for primary actions, form submissions, dialog confirmations, and any interaction that performs an operation. Choose the variant that matches the action's importance and tone.
button.whenNotToUse: Do not use for navigation between pages or views. Use a Link component or anchor element instead. Do not use for toggling state; use Toggle or Switch.

values.description: Standard button for primary page actions.
For irreversible actions like delete. Uses destructive color tokens.
Bordered button for secondary actions that need clear affordance.
De-emphasized button for supplementary actions.
Minimal button for toolbar actions or inline controls. No background until hovered.
Renders as a text link. Use for inline navigation-like actions within prose.

variant.description: Visual treatment. Use destructive for irreversible actions, ghost for toolbar actions, link for inline text actions.

values.description: Standard size, suitable for most contexts.
Compact size for dense UIs or inline actions.
Large size for prominent calls to action.
Square aspect ratio for icon-only buttons.

size.description: Button size. Use icon for square icon-only buttons.

disabled.description: Whether the button is non-interactive. Conveys that the action is unavailable.

asChild.description: When true, merges props and behavior onto the child element instead of rendering a <button>. Used for composing with router Link components.

keyboardInteractions.description: Activates the button.
Activates the button.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the button contains only an icon and no visible text
requiredAttributes.description: Provide a text description of the button's action for screen readers.

constraints.context: An action that submits a form, confirms a dialog, or triggers a side effect
constraints.rule: Use Button

constraints.context: Navigation between pages or views
constraints.rule: Use a Link component or anchor element instead of Button

constraints.context: Toggling a boolean state (on/off, show/hide)
constraints.rule: Use Toggle or Switch instead of Button

constraints.context: A destructive or irreversible action
constraints.rule: Use the destructive variant

alert-dialog.name: Alert Dialog
alert-dialog.description: A modal dialog that interrupts the user with important content and expects a response. Built on Radix UI AlertDialog. Renders with a required action and a cancel option. The user cannot dismiss it by clicking the overlay or pressing Escape — they must choose an explicit action.
alert-dialog.whenToUse: Use for confirming destructive or irreversible actions: deleting records, discarding unsaved changes, revoking access. Use when the consequence of proceeding is significant enough that the user should explicitly acknowledge it.
alert-dialog.whenNotToUse: Do not use for informational messages or non-destructive confirmations. Use Dialog for those. Do not use when the user should be able to dismiss without choosing — that is what Dialog provides.

open.description: Controlled open state of the dialog.

onOpenChange.description: Callback fired when the open state changes.

requiredAttributes.description: Must reference the AlertDialogTitle element.
Must reference the AlertDialogDescription element.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves focus between focusable elements within the dialog. Focus is trapped inside.
Does NOT close the dialog. User must select an explicit action.
Activates the focused button.
Activates the focused button.

accessibility.focusManagement: On open, focus moves to the cancel button (least destructive action). On close, focus returns to the trigger element. Focus is trapped within the dialog while open.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogTrigger
subComponents.description: The element that opens the alert dialog.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogContent
subComponents.description: The container for the dialog's content, rendered in a portal.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogHeader
subComponents.description: Groups the title and description at the top of the dialog.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogTitle
subComponents.description: The title of the alert dialog. Rendered as an h2. Referenced by aria-labelledby.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogDescription
subComponents.description: A description providing additional context about the alert. Referenced by aria-describedby.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogFooter
subComponents.description: Contains the action and cancel buttons.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogAction
subComponents.description: The button that confirms the destructive action.

subComponents.name: AlertDialogCancel
subComponents.description: The button that cancels and closes the dialog.

composition.notes: AlertDialogContent must contain AlertDialogTitle and AlertDialogDescription for accessibility. AlertDialogAction and AlertDialogCancel must appear in AlertDialogFooter. Place cancel before confirm in reading order.

constraints.context: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action
constraints.rule: Use AlertDialog instead of Dialog

constraints.context: Informational messages or non-destructive confirmations
constraints.rule: Use Dialog instead of AlertDialog

constraints.context: Cases where the user should be able to dismiss without choosing an action
constraints.rule: Use Dialog instead of AlertDialog

dialog.name: Dialog
dialog.description: A modal window that appears over the page content. Built on Radix UI Dialog. Can be dismissed by clicking the overlay, pressing Escape, or activating a close button.
dialog.whenToUse: Use for forms, settings panels, detail views, or any content that benefits from focused attention without leaving the current page. Appropriate when the user should be able to dismiss the content without taking an action.
dialog.whenNotToUse: Do not use for confirming destructive actions. Use AlertDialog instead — it prevents accidental dismissal. Do not use for simple, brief messages; use a toast or inline alert.

open.description: Controlled open state of the dialog.

onOpenChange.description: Callback fired when the open state changes.

modal.description: Whether the dialog blocks interaction with the rest of the page.

requiredAttributes.description: Must reference the DialogTitle element.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves focus between focusable elements within the dialog. Focus is trapped inside.
Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger.
Activates the focused interactive element.

accessibility.focusManagement: On open, focus moves to the first focusable element inside the dialog. On close, focus returns to the trigger element. Focus is trapped within the dialog while open.

subComponents.name: DialogTrigger
subComponents.description: The element that opens the dialog.

subComponents.name: DialogContent
subComponents.description: The container for the dialog's content, rendered in a portal.

subComponents.name: DialogHeader
subComponents.description: Groups the title and description at the top of the dialog.

subComponents.name: DialogTitle
subComponents.description: The title of the dialog. Referenced by aria-labelledby.

subComponents.name: DialogDescription
subComponents.description: A description providing additional context.

subComponents.name: DialogFooter
subComponents.description: Contains action buttons.

subComponents.name: DialogClose
subComponents.description: A button that closes the dialog.

constraints.context: Forms, settings panels, or detail views requiring focused attention
constraints.rule: Use Dialog

constraints.context: Confirming destructive actions
constraints.rule: Use AlertDialog instead of Dialog

card.name: Card
card.description: A container for grouping related content and actions. Provides visual separation through a bordered surface.
card.whenToUse: Use to group related information into a distinct visual unit. Appropriate for dashboard widgets, summary panels, list items with detail, or any content that benefits from visual containment.
card.whenNotToUse: Do not nest Cards inside other Cards. If content hierarchy is needed, use headings and spacing within a single Card. Do not use as a clickable element — wrap content in an interactive element instead.

subComponents.name: CardHeader
subComponents.description: Contains the title and optional description at the top of the card.

subComponents.name: CardTitle
subComponents.description: The title of the card.

subComponents.name: CardDescription
subComponents.description: A description below the title.

subComponents.name: CardContent
subComponents.description: The main content area of the card.

subComponents.name: CardFooter
subComponents.description: Contains action buttons or supplementary information.

constraints.context: Nesting Cards inside other Cards
constraints.rule: Use headings and spacing within a single Card instead

constraints.context: A clickable surface
constraints.rule: Wrap Card content in an interactive element; do not make Card itself clickable

input.name: Input
input.description: A single-line text input field built on the native <input> element. Supports all standard HTML input types.
input.whenToUse: Use for short-form text entry: names, email addresses, search queries, numeric values. Choose the appropriate HTML type attribute for the content (email, password, number, etc.).
input.whenNotToUse: Do not use for multi-line text. Use Textarea instead. Do not use for selecting from a predefined set of options; use Select or RadioGroup.

type.description: HTML input type (text, email, password, number, search, etc.).

placeholder.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

requiredAttributes.description: Required for associating the input with its <label> element via htmlFor.

accessibility.notes: Every Input must have an associated <label> element. The label must be visible, not just provided via aria-label. Placeholder text is not a substitute for a label.

constraints.context: Multi-line text entry
constraints.rule: Use Textarea instead of Input

constraints.context: Selecting from a predefined set of options
constraints.rule: Use Select or RadioGroup instead of Input

badge.name: Badge
badge.description: A small label for categorization, status indication, or metadata. Renders as an inline element.
badge.whenToUse: Use to display status (active, pending, archived), categories, tags, or counts. Appropriate for metadata that should be scannable at a glance.
badge.whenNotToUse: Do not use as a button or interactive element. If the badge should trigger an action, wrap it in a button or use a different component.

values.description: Standard badge for general categorization.
De-emphasized badge for supplementary metadata.
Bordered badge for subtle labeling.
Indicates errors or critical status.

variant.description: Visual treatment. Use destructive to indicate errors or critical status.

accessibility.notes: Badge is a presentational element. If the badge conveys status that is not also communicated through surrounding text, use aria-label on the badge or ensure the status is programmatically determinable through other means.

dropdown-menu.name: Dropdown Menu
dropdown-menu.description: A menu that appears on activation of a trigger element. Built on Radix UI DropdownMenu. Supports items, checkboxes, radio groups, sub-menus, separators, and keyboard navigation.
dropdown-menu.whenToUse: Use when a set of actions or options needs to be accessible from a single trigger without taking up permanent screen space. Appropriate for overflow menus, context-sensitive actions, and settings with multiple choices.
dropdown-menu.whenNotToUse: Do not use for navigation — use a navigation menu or links. Do not use when the options should always be visible; use RadioGroup or a set of Buttons instead.

onOpenChange.description: Callback fired when the open state changes.

modal.description: Whether the menu blocks interaction with the rest of the page.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves focus to the next menu item.
Moves focus to the previous menu item.
Activates the focused menu item.
Activates the focused menu item.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.

accessibility.focusManagement: On open, focus moves to the first menu item. On close, focus returns to the trigger. Arrow keys cycle through items.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuTrigger
subComponents.description: The element that opens the dropdown menu.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuContent
subComponents.description: The container for menu items, rendered in a portal.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuItem
subComponents.description: A single actionable item in the menu.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
subComponents.description: A menu item that can be toggled on/off.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuRadioGroup
subComponents.description: Groups radio items for mutually exclusive selection.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuRadioItem
subComponents.description: A radio-style menu item for single selection within a group.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuLabel
subComponents.description: A non-interactive label for grouping menu items.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuSeparator
subComponents.description: A visual divider between groups of items.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuGroup
subComponents.description: Groups related menu items together.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuSub
subComponents.description: A container for a sub-menu.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuSubTrigger
subComponents.description: The item that opens a sub-menu on hover or keyboard navigation.

subComponents.name: DropdownMenuSubContent
subComponents.description: The content container for a sub-menu.

table.name: Table
table.description: A set of primitives for presenting tabular data with a meaningful row-and-column relationship. These are thin, presentational wrappers over the native table elements — Table renders a <table> inside a horizontally scrollable container, and the sub-components render thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, th, td, and caption. There is no built-in sorting, filtering, pagination, or selection; those are composed on top.
table.whenToUse: Use to display data where each row is a record and each column is a comparable attribute: members and their roles, invoices, audit logs, permission lists. Reach for Table whenever the relationship between rows and columns carries meaning that assistive technology should be able to announce.
table.whenNotToUse: Do not use Table to lay out or align non-tabular content — use CSS grid or flexbox for layout. Do not use a table to present a single record's key/value pairs; use a description list (dl) or a Card instead. For large interactive datasets, still use these primitives for markup but drive state with a headless table library rather than building a bespoke component.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every TableHead (th) cell
requiredAttributes.description: Set scope="col" for column headers and scope="row" for row headers so screen readers can associate each data cell with its header. Header cells must be th elements, not styled td cells.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the TableHead (th) of a sortable column
requiredAttributes.description: Reflect the column's current sort state as ascending, descending, or none. Only one column may expose a non-none value at a time so the active sort is unambiguous.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the table has no visible TableCaption and no aria-labelledby reference
requiredAttributes.description: Give the table an accessible name with a literal label string so its purpose is announced when it receives focus or is navigated. Prefer a visible TableCaption where one is appropriate.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the table has no visible TableCaption but an existing on-page heading names it
requiredAttributes.description: Reference the id of the visible element that already names the table, instead of duplicating the name in an aria-label. Use either aria-labelledby or aria-label, not both.

accessibility.notes: Preserve the native semantic structure: real thead, tbody, tfoot, th, and td elements — never reconstruct a table from styled divs, which strips the row/column semantics screen readers depend on. Do NOT use Table for visual layout, alignment, or positioning; that is the job of CSS grid or flexbox. Provide an accessible name through TableCaption (preferred) or aria-label/aria-labelledby. A sortable column header must be a real Button inside the th, with the th carrying aria-sort, so the control is keyboard-operable and announced as a button.

subComponents.name: TableHeader
subComponents.description: The table's header section, rendered as a thead. Contains the header TableRow whose cells are TableHead elements.

subComponents.name: TableBody
subComponents.description: The table's body section, rendered as a tbody. Contains the data TableRows.

subComponents.name: TableFooter
subComponents.description: The table's footer section, rendered as a tfoot. Use for summary rows such as totals.

subComponents.name: TableRow
subComponents.description: A single row, rendered as a tr. Lives inside TableHeader, TableBody, or TableFooter and contains TableHead or TableCell elements.

subComponents.name: TableHead
subComponents.description: A header cell, rendered as a th. Carries scope and, when its column is sortable, aria-sort and a Button that toggles the sort.

subComponents.name: TableCell
subComponents.description: A data cell, rendered as a td. May contain plain text or interactive controls such as a Badge or a row actions menu.

subComponents.name: TableCaption
subComponents.description: An accessible caption, rendered as a caption. Describes the table's contents and supplies its accessible name.

composition.notes: TableRow must appear inside TableHeader, TableBody, or TableFooter — not directly under Table. Header cells use TableHead (th); data cells use TableCell (td). When present, TableCaption is the first child of Table. These primitives carry no data behavior; compose sorting, filtering, pagination, and selection on top of them.

constraints.context: Displaying data with a meaningful row-and-column relationship
constraints.rule: Use Table with semantic TableHeader/TableBody and TableHead/TableCell elements

constraints.context: Visual layout, alignment, or positioning of non-tabular content
constraints.rule: Use CSS grid or flexbox instead of Table

constraints.context: Column and row header cells
constraints.rule: Use TableHead (th) with an explicit scope attribute rather than a styled TableCell (td)

constraints.context: A sortable column
constraints.rule: Expose the sort state with aria-sort on the TableHead and make the trigger a real Button

constraints.context: Sorting, filtering, pagination, or row selection over large datasets
constraints.rule: Compose a headless table library such as TanStack Table on top of these primitives instead of hand-rolling the state

constraints.context: Any data table
constraints.rule: Give the table an accessible name describing its contents — a TableCaption (preferred), or aria-label/aria-labelledby

popover.name: Popover
popover.description: A non-modal floating panel anchored to a trigger, rendered in a portal. Built on Radix UI Popover. The content element carries role="dialog" and the trigger carries aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded, and aria-controls. Unlike Dialog, it is non-modal by default: focus is not trapped, the page behind stays scrollable and interactive, and the rest of the page is not hidden from assistive technology.
popover.whenToUse: Use for rich, interactive content that belongs to a specific control and should appear next to it: a date picker, a column-visibility menu, a filter builder, a small edit form, a combobox surface. Reach for Popover when the content is transient, contains focusable elements, and the user should be able to keep working with the page around it.
popover.whenNotToUse: Do not use for plain descriptive text on hover — use Tooltip, which is announced via aria-describedby and costs no interaction. Do not use for content that must be dealt with before the user continues; use Dialog, which is modal and traps focus. Do not use for a list of commands or actions; use DropdownMenu, which implements the menu pattern with roving focus and typeahead. Do not use for large or edge-anchored panels such as navigation or detail drawers; use Sheet.

open.description: On Popover (root). Controlled open state. Pair with onOpenChange; omit both to let the component manage its own state.

defaultOpen.description: On Popover (root). Initial open state for uncontrolled usage. Do not combine with open.

onOpenChange.description: On Popover (root). Callback fired when the open state changes, including when the popover closes via Escape or an outside pointer press.

modal.description: On Popover (root). When false (the default) focus is not trapped, outside pointer events pass through, and the page keeps scrolling. When true, focus is trapped inside the content, outside pointer events are disabled, the rest of the page is marked aria-hidden, and scroll is locked. Set true only when the popover's task must be completed or abandoned before anything else.

values.description: Open above the anchor. Use when the trigger sits near the bottom of the viewport or above a long form.
Open to the right of the anchor. Use for triggers in a left rail or the start of a row.
Open below the anchor. The default, and the right choice for toolbar and field-adjacent triggers.
Open to the left of the anchor. Use for triggers in a right rail or the end of a row.

side.description: On PopoverContent. Preferred edge of the anchor to open against. This is a preference, not a guarantee — with avoidCollisions left on, the popover flips to the opposite side when the preferred side would overflow the viewport.

values.description: Align the content's start edge with the anchor's start edge. Use for wide content hanging off a narrow left-aligned trigger.
Center the content on the anchor. The shadcn default.
Align the content's end edge with the anchor's end edge. Use for right-aligned triggers so the panel does not overhang the viewport.

align.description: On PopoverContent. Alignment along the perpendicular axis of side. shadcn's PopoverContent sets this to center explicitly, matching the Radix default.

sideOffset.description: On PopoverContent. Distance in pixels between the anchor and the content along the side axis. shadcn overrides the Radix default of 0 to 4 so the panel's shadow reads as separate from the trigger.

alignOffset.description: On PopoverContent. Offset in pixels along the alignment axis. Use to nudge the panel into optical alignment with an icon trigger; prefer changing align first.

avoidCollisions.description: On PopoverContent. When true the popover flips and shifts to stay inside the viewport. Leave enabled; disabling it will let the panel render partly offscreen on small viewports.

collisionPadding.description: On PopoverContent. Minimum distance in pixels to keep from the collision boundary. Raise it when a sticky header or bottom bar would otherwise sit on top of the panel.

asChild.description: On PopoverTrigger and PopoverAnchor. Merges props and behavior onto the single child element instead of rendering the default element. Use asChild on PopoverTrigger to make a Button the trigger without nesting a button inside a button.

requiredAttributes.condition: always, on PopoverContent
requiredAttributes.description: Radix Popover has no Title part, so nothing is wired automatically. Give PopoverTitle an id and reference it from PopoverContent's aria-labelledby, or supply aria-label on PopoverContent when there is no visible title. Without one of these the panel is announced only as "dialog".

requiredAttributes.condition: when PopoverDescription is present
requiredAttributes.description: Also unwired by default. Give PopoverDescription an id and reference it from PopoverContent so the supporting copy is announced on open.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the trigger is icon-only
requiredAttributes.description: Name the trigger by the panel it opens, for example "Filter options", not by the icon.

keyboardInteractions.description: On the trigger, opens the popover. Inside the content, activates the focused control.
On the trigger, opens the popover.
Moves to the next focusable element. When non-modal (the default) focus leaves the popover and continues into the page; when modal, focus wraps within the content.
Moves to the previous focusable element, with the same non-modal versus modal difference as Tab.
Closes the popover and returns focus to PopoverTrigger.

accessibility.focusManagement: On open, focus moves into the content. On close, focus returns to PopoverTrigger. Focus is trapped only when modal is true; in the default non-modal mode Tab walks out of the panel into the rest of the page, which is why the panel must not hold a task that has to be finished before the user moves on.
accessibility.notes: PopoverHeader, PopoverTitle, and PopoverDescription are plain presentational elements in shadcn's implementation — a div, a div, and a p. They are not Radix parts and carry no ARIA wiring, unlike DialogTitle and DialogDescription. Rendering a PopoverTitle therefore does not give the panel an accessible name; the aria-labelledby link must be authored by hand. Because the default mode is non-modal, screen reader users can navigate away from an open popover with no warning; do not rely on the panel holding their attention.

subComponents.name: PopoverTrigger
subComponents.description: The control that toggles the popover. Renders a button and receives aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded, and aria-controls automatically. Use asChild to project this behavior onto a Button.

subComponents.name: PopoverContent
subComponents.description: The floating panel, portalled to the document body and positioned against the anchor. Owns side, align, sideOffset, alignOffset, and the collision props, and is the element that must carry aria-labelledby or aria-label.

subComponents.name: PopoverAnchor
subComponents.description: An optional alternative positioning reference. When present, PopoverContent positions against the anchor instead of the trigger. Use it when the visual origin of the panel differs from the control that opens it — anchoring a combobox list to the whole input while a chevron button triggers it, for example. Must be a descendant of the same Popover root.

subComponents.name: PopoverHeader
subComponents.description: Groups the title and description at the top of the panel. A presentational div with no ARIA semantics.

subComponents.name: PopoverTitle
subComponents.description: The panel's visible title. A presentational element, not a Radix part — give it an id and reference it from PopoverContent's aria-labelledby to make it the accessible name.

subComponents.name: PopoverDescription
subComponents.description: Supporting copy beneath the title. A presentational p element — reference its id from PopoverContent's aria-describedby to have it announced.

composition.notes: Positioning props live on PopoverContent, never on the Popover root; open state props live on the root, never on the content. PopoverContent portals itself, so no explicit Portal sub-component is exported or needed. PopoverAnchor, when used, replaces the trigger as the positioning reference but not as the control — the trigger still opens the panel. PopoverHeader, PopoverTitle, and PopoverDescription were added to the shadcn registry after the original three-part API; older installs may only export Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent, and PopoverAnchor.

constraints.context: Transient interactive content anchored to a specific control, such as a date picker or filter panel
constraints.rule: Use Popover

constraints.context: Any PopoverContent
constraints.rule: Give the panel an accessible name by wiring aria-labelledby to the PopoverTitle's id, or by setting aria-label — Radix Popover does not wire this automatically

constraints.context: Plain descriptive text shown on hover or focus
constraints.rule: Use Tooltip instead of Popover

constraints.context: Content the user must act on before continuing, or that would leave the app in an inconsistent state if abandoned
constraints.rule: Use Dialog instead of Popover, or set modal on Popover — the default non-modal popover lets focus and pointer input leave freely

constraints.context: A list of commands or actions
constraints.rule: Use DropdownMenu instead of Popover so the menu pattern, roving focus, and typeahead come for free

constraints.context: Positioning a popover with side, align, sideOffset, or the collision props
constraints.rule: Set these on PopoverContent, not on the Popover root, where they have no effect

constraints.context: An icon-only PopoverTrigger
constraints.rule: Give the trigger an aria-label naming the panel it opens

constraints.context: A trigger that is already a Button or other interactive element
constraints.rule: Use asChild on PopoverTrigger rather than nesting the control inside it, which would produce a button within a button

constraints.context: Small viewports where the panel would overflow
constraints.rule: Leave avoidCollisions enabled and consider Sheet for content that cannot fit as a floating panel

popover.notes: Overlap to disambiguate later: Popover, Dialog, Sheet, DropdownMenu, and Tooltip all render portalled content above the page, and nothing in the type system stops an author from using any of them for the same job. The distinctions that matter are modality (Popover is non-modal by default, Dialog and Sheet are modal), anchoring (Popover and Tooltip position against a trigger; Dialog and Sheet position against the viewport), and interactivity (Tooltip content is unreachable, Popover content is fully interactive). A governance rule should later select on those axes rather than on component identity — for example, flagging interactive controls inside Tooltip content, and flagging a Popover carrying a form with a submit action that ought to be a Dialog. Token note: this entry references popover and popover-foreground, which are real shadcn theme variables (--popover, --popover-foreground) but are not yet present in this pack's token registry; they should be registered rather than substituted with background and foreground, which would misdescribe the component.

tooltip.name: Tooltip
tooltip.description: A small text label that appears on hover or keyboard focus to describe the control it is attached to. Built on Radix UI Tooltip. The content carries role="tooltip" and is linked to the trigger with aria-describedby while open. It is supplementary by definition: it does not receive focus, it closes on click and on pointer-down, and it never opens from touch input.
tooltip.whenToUse: Use to name or clarify a control whose purpose is not fully carried by its visible presentation — an icon-only button, a truncated cell, an abbreviated column header, a disabled control whose reason for being disabled needs explaining. Keep the content to a short phrase.
tooltip.whenNotToUse: Do not use for anything the user actually needs. Tooltip content is unreachable on touch devices and disappears on click, so information that is required to complete a task must live in the page, in a Popover, or in helper text. Do not put links, buttons, form fields, or any focusable element inside a tooltip — they cannot be reached. Do not use a tooltip as a control's only accessible name if the control is not the trigger itself.

delayDuration.description: On TooltipProvider and Tooltip (root). Milliseconds of hover before the tooltip opens. shadcn overrides the Radix default of 700 to 0 on its TooltipProvider, so tooltips appear immediately. Set a non-zero value on the provider when instant tooltips feel noisy across a dense UI; set it on an individual Tooltip to override the provider for one case.

skipDelayDuration.description: On TooltipProvider. Milliseconds during which moving to another trigger opens its tooltip with no delay. This is what makes sweeping across a toolbar feel continuous rather than stuttering.

disableHoverableContent.description: On TooltipProvider and Tooltip (root). When true the tooltip closes as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger, instead of staying open while the pointer travels onto the content. Leave false so users can move onto long content to read it.

open.description: On Tooltip (root). Controlled open state. Use sparingly — forcing a tooltip open bypasses the hover and focus semantics screen reader and touch users depend on.

defaultOpen.description: On Tooltip (root). Initial open state for uncontrolled usage.

onOpenChange.description: On Tooltip (root). Callback fired when the open state changes.

values.description: Open above the trigger. The default, and the safest choice because it does not cover the content below the control.
Open to the right. Use for triggers in a collapsed left navigation rail.
Open below the trigger. Use for controls in a top app bar where a top-side tooltip would clip.
Open to the left. Use for triggers at the right edge of a row or toolbar.

side.description: On TooltipContent. Preferred edge of the trigger to open against. With avoidCollisions on, the tooltip flips to the opposite side rather than overflowing the viewport.

values.description: Align to the trigger's start edge. Use when the label is much wider than a small trigger at the start of a row.
Center on the trigger. The default and the right choice for icon buttons.
Align to the trigger's end edge. Use for triggers near the end of a row.

align.description: On TooltipContent. Alignment along the perpendicular axis of side.

sideOffset.description: On TooltipContent. Distance in pixels from the trigger. shadcn sets 0 because its TooltipContent renders a built-in arrow that visually bridges the gap.

alignOffset.description: On TooltipContent. Offset in pixels along the alignment axis.

avoidCollisions.description: On TooltipContent. When true the tooltip flips and shifts to stay inside the viewport. Leave enabled.

aria-label.description: On TooltipContent. Replaces the visible content in the accessibility tree with this string, rendered into a visually hidden element that carries role="tooltip". Use only when the visible content does not read well when announced — for example a formatted value where the spoken form should differ. Setting it removes role="tooltip" from the visible element.

asChild.description: On TooltipTrigger. Merges the trigger behavior onto the single child element instead of rendering a button. Use it to attach a tooltip to an existing Button without nesting one button inside another.

requiredAttributes.condition: wired automatically by Radix while the tooltip is open
requiredAttributes.description: Radix sets aria-describedby on the trigger, pointing at the content id. This makes the tooltip a description, not a name — an icon-only button still needs its own accessible name from aria-label or visually hidden text.

requiredAttributes.condition: on an icon-only trigger
requiredAttributes.description: Name the control itself. Do not rely on the tooltip to supply the name: description and name are announced differently, and the tooltip is entirely absent for touch users.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moving focus to the trigger opens the tooltip immediately, bypassing delayDuration. Moving focus away closes it.
Closes the tooltip while leaving focus on the trigger.
Closes the tooltip, because activating the trigger dismisses it.
Closes the tooltip, because activating the trigger dismisses it.

accessibility.focusManagement: The tooltip never takes focus — focus stays on the trigger the whole time it is open, and the content is not in the tab order. This is exactly why interactive content inside a tooltip is unreachable. The trigger must itself be focusable: a natively disabled button fires no focus or pointer events, so wrap it in a focusable element or mark it aria-disabled with the control still focusable if the tooltip needs to explain why it is unavailable.
accessibility.notes: Radix explicitly ignores pointer events whose pointerType is "touch", so a tooltip never opens from a tap or a touch hover — on phones and tablets the content simply does not exist. Pointer-down and click also close it. Treat every tooltip as decoration over information already available elsewhere. Because the content is linked with aria-describedby, it is announced after the control's name and role; a control whose name comes only from its tooltip will be announced as unnamed to some users and as nothing at all on touch.

subComponents.name: TooltipProvider
subComponents.description: Supplies shared timing context — delayDuration, skipDelayDuration, disableHoverableContent — to every Tooltip beneath it. Mount it once near the application root. It is not optional: a Tooltip rendered outside a provider throws, because Radix creates the provider context with no default value.

subComponents.name: TooltipTrigger
subComponents.description: The control the tooltip describes. Renders a button and receives aria-describedby while open. Use asChild to attach the behavior to an existing Button or other focusable control.

subComponents.name: TooltipContent
subComponents.description: The floating label, portalled to the document body and carrying role="tooltip". shadcn's implementation renders a built-in arrow inside it, so no separate Arrow sub-component is exported. Accepts short text only — it is not reachable by keyboard or touch.

composition.notes: TooltipProvider is an ancestor, not a sibling: wrap the application once rather than wrapping each Tooltip, so skipDelayDuration can do its job across adjacent triggers. Positioning props live on TooltipContent; timing props live on TooltipProvider or the Tooltip root. shadcn's TooltipContent already includes the Radix Arrow, so do not add one.

constraints.context: Clarifying an icon-only button, a truncated label, or an abbreviated header
constraints.rule: Use Tooltip with short text content

constraints.context: Any application rendering a Tooltip
constraints.rule: Mount a single TooltipProvider at the application root — Tooltip throws when rendered outside one

constraints.context: Links, buttons, form fields, or any focusable element inside tooltip content
constraints.rule: Move the interactive content into a Popover — tooltip content never receives focus and closes on click, so those controls are unreachable

constraints.context: Information a user needs in order to complete a task
constraints.rule: Do not put it only in a Tooltip — it is entirely absent on touch devices; put it in the page, in helper text, or in a Popover

constraints.context: An icon-only control with a tooltip
constraints.rule: Give the control its own accessible name with aria-label or visually hidden text; the tooltip supplies aria-describedby, which is a description and not a name

constraints.context: A tooltip on a disabled control
constraints.rule: Keep the trigger focusable — use aria-disabled with the control still in the tab order, or wrap it, because a natively disabled button emits no pointer or focus events and the tooltip will never open

constraints.context: Tooltip content longer than a short phrase
constraints.rule: Use a Popover instead, so the content can be read at the user's pace and reached by keyboard

constraints.context: A trigger that is already a Button or other interactive element
constraints.rule: Use asChild on TooltipTrigger rather than nesting the control inside it

tooltip.notes: Overlap to disambiguate later: Tooltip and Popover are both trigger-anchored portalled overlays and are frequently interchanged by mistake. The dividing line is reachability, not size — tooltip content cannot be focused, is dismissed by click, and is never shown to touch users, so anything load-bearing or interactive belongs in a Popover. A governance rule should later assert that TooltipContent's subtree contains no interactive-category component and no focusable element, and should flag a Tooltip whose content is the only place a piece of information appears. Token note: shadcn's TooltipContent inverts the surface, using bg-foreground with text-background rather than a dedicated tooltip token pair, so the tokens listed here are deliberately the base semantic colors and not a popover-style pair.

sheet.name: Sheet
sheet.description: A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the viewport. Built on the same Radix UI Dialog primitive as Dialog — same modality, same focus trap, same dismissal behavior — differing only in that its content is pinned to a viewport edge rather than centered, and sized to that edge. Renders an overlay and, by default, a close button in the corner of the panel.
sheet.whenToUse: Use for a focused task or detail view that needs more room than a Popover and benefits from staying visually connected to the edge it came from: mobile navigation, a filters panel, a record's detail or edit view, a settings drawer. The left and right sides suit navigation and long forms; the bottom side suits mobile action panels.
sheet.whenNotToUse: Do not use for confirming a destructive action — use AlertDialog, which cannot be dismissed by accident. Do not use for a short message or a small form that fits in a centered window; Dialog is the more conventional choice and demands less travel from the user's eye. Do not use for content anchored to a specific control, such as a picker or a small menu; use Popover or DropdownMenu. Do not use for brief status feedback; use a toast.

open.description: On Sheet (root). Controlled open state. Pair with onOpenChange.

defaultOpen.description: On Sheet (root). Initial open state for uncontrolled usage.

onOpenChange.description: On Sheet (root). Callback fired when the open state changes, including dismissal via Escape, the overlay, or the close button. Use it to reset panel state so a reopened sheet does not show stale input.

modal.description: On Sheet (root). When true (the default) focus is trapped in the panel, the rest of the page is hidden from assistive technology, and outside pointer events are blocked. Setting it false breaks the expectation the overlay sets — the page still looks dimmed and unavailable while remaining interactive.

values.description: Slide in from the right edge, full height, capped near 24rem on larger viewports. The default, and the conventional place for detail and edit panels in left-to-right layouts.
Slide in from the left edge, full height. Use for navigation, which users expect on the side the primary nav already occupies.
Slide down from the top edge, height sized to content. Use sparingly — it collides with system and browser chrome and with sticky headers.
Slide up from the bottom edge, height sized to content. The most reachable option on phones, where the top of the screen is far from the thumb.

side.description: On SheetContent. Which viewport edge the panel is pinned to and animates from. Left and right panels are full height; top and bottom panels size to their content.

showCloseButton.description: On SheetContent. Renders the built-in close button in the panel's top-right corner, an icon button with visually hidden "Close" text. Set false only when supplying an explicit SheetClose elsewhere in the panel — never to remove the visible dismissal affordance entirely.

onEscapeKeyDown.description: On SheetContent. Fires when Escape is pressed. Call preventDefault to keep the sheet open — do this only to confirm discarding unsaved work, never to make the panel undismissable.

onInteractOutside.description: On SheetContent. Fires when the user interacts outside the panel, including on the overlay. Call preventDefault to suppress accidental dismissal of a partially completed form, and pair it with a confirmation path.

asChild.description: On SheetTrigger and SheetClose. Merges props and behavior onto the single child element. Use it to make an existing Button open or close the sheet without nesting a button inside a button.

requiredAttributes.condition: satisfied by rendering SheetTitle
requiredAttributes.description: SheetTitle is Radix's Dialog.Title, so rendering it wires aria-labelledby automatically. A sheet without one is announced unnamed, and Radix logs a development warning. When the design has no visible title, still render SheetTitle inside a visually hidden wrapper.

requiredAttributes.condition: satisfied by rendering SheetDescription, or explicitly opted out
requiredAttributes.description: SheetDescription is Radix's Dialog.Description and wires aria-describedby automatically. If the panel genuinely has no description, pass aria-describedby={undefined} to SheetContent to silence the Radix warning rather than adding filler text.

keyboardInteractions.description: On the trigger, opens the sheet. Inside the panel, activates the focused control.
On the trigger, opens the sheet.
Moves focus to the next focusable element inside the panel. Focus is trapped and wraps at the end.
Moves focus to the previous focusable element inside the panel, wrapping at the start.
Closes the sheet and returns focus to SheetTrigger.

accessibility.focusManagement: On open, focus moves into the panel — to the first focusable element, which is usually the built-in close button. On close, focus returns to SheetTrigger. Focus is trapped inside the panel and the rest of the page is marked aria-hidden while open, so a screen reader user cannot wander out of it. When the sheet is opened programmatically rather than by a trigger, set focus deliberately on close, because there is no trigger to return to.
accessibility.notes: Because a Sheet is a Radix Dialog, all of Dialog's accessibility obligations apply unchanged. The panel is a scroll container in its own right; long content must scroll inside the panel rather than the page, and a footer with the primary action should stay reachable without scrolling past it. On small viewports a left or right sheet occupies three quarters of the width, so it is effectively full screen — check that the close affordance is inside the safe area.

subComponents.name: SheetTrigger
subComponents.description: The control that opens the sheet. Renders a button; use asChild to project the behavior onto an existing Button.

subComponents.name: SheetContent
subComponents.description: The sliding panel. Renders its own portal and overlay internally, owns the side and showCloseButton props, and lays out as a flex column so SheetFooter can be pushed to the bottom.

subComponents.name: SheetHeader
subComponents.description: Groups the title and description at the top of the panel. A presentational div that supplies padding and spacing.

subComponents.name: SheetTitle
subComponents.description: The panel's title. This is Radix's Dialog.Title, so rendering it gives the sheet its accessible name via aria-labelledby. Required for an accessible sheet — hide it visually rather than omitting it.

subComponents.name: SheetDescription
subComponents.description: Supporting copy beneath the title. This is Radix's Dialog.Description and wires aria-describedby automatically. Omit it only alongside aria-describedby={undefined} on SheetContent.

subComponents.name: SheetFooter
subComponents.description: Holds the panel's actions. A presentational div with an auto top margin, so it settles at the bottom of the panel regardless of content height.

subComponents.name: SheetClose
subComponents.description: A control that closes the sheet. Use it for an explicit Cancel or Done button in SheetFooter, with asChild to wrap a Button. Distinct from the built-in corner close button that SheetContent renders when showCloseButton is true.

composition.notes: SheetContent renders the portal and overlay itself; shadcn defines SheetPortal and SheetOverlay in the same file but does not export them, so they cannot be composed or overridden from outside. SheetTitle and SheetDescription belong inside SheetHeader, and SheetClose inside SheetFooter, though neither nesting is enforced. Because SheetContent is a flex column with a footer that has margin-top auto, scrolling regions should be placed as a middle child rather than wrapping the whole panel. The side prop lives on SheetContent, not on the Sheet root.

constraints.context: A focused task or detail view needing more room than a Popover, such as mobile navigation, filters, or a record editor
constraints.rule: Use Sheet

constraints.context: Any SheetContent
constraints.rule: Render a SheetTitle, visually hidden if the design has no visible title, so the panel has an accessible name

constraints.context: A sheet with no description
constraints.rule: Pass aria-describedby={undefined} to SheetContent rather than adding filler description text

constraints.context: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action
constraints.rule: Use AlertDialog instead of Sheet

constraints.context: Content anchored to a specific control, such as a picker, filter panel, or action list
constraints.rule: Use Popover or DropdownMenu instead of Sheet

constraints.context: Choosing the edge for a mobile action panel
constraints.rule: Use side="bottom" so the panel and its actions fall within thumb reach

constraints.context: Primary navigation revealed on small viewports
constraints.rule: Use side="left" or side="right" to match the side the navigation occupies on larger viewports

constraints.context: Suppressing dismissal with onEscapeKeyDown or onInteractOutside
constraints.rule: Do this only to confirm discarding unsaved work, and always leave a visible way to close the panel

constraints.context: Hiding the built-in close button with showCloseButton={false}
constraints.rule: Provide an explicit SheetClose elsewhere in the panel

constraints.context: A sheet whose content exceeds the panel height
constraints.rule: Scroll inside the panel and keep the footer actions reachable, rather than letting the page behind scroll

sheet.notes: Overlap to disambiguate later: Sheet is the Radix Dialog primitive with edge-anchored positioning — the sub-component sets are one-to-one (Trigger, Content, Header, Title, Description, Footer, Close) and the accessibility contract is identical, so nothing structural distinguishes a Sheet from a Dialog. The choice between them is presentational and contextual: viewport size, how much room the task needs, and whether the panel should read as attached to a page edge. AlertDialog is the one genuine behavioral distinction in this family, because it refuses dismissal by Escape or overlay. A governance rule should later encode: destructive confirmation must be AlertDialog, never Sheet or Dialog; a modal overlay carrying navigation or a long form should prefer Sheet; a short confirmation or small form should prefer Dialog; and an author should not nest a Sheet inside a Dialog or another Sheet, since stacked focus traps have no defined return path. Because Sheet, Dialog, and AlertDialog share prop names and sub-component shapes, that rule should key on intent and content, not on prop values.

field.name: Field
field.description: The family of layout and labeling primitives shadcn ships for composing form fields: Field wraps one control with its label, helper text, and validation message; FieldSet and FieldLegend give a set of related controls real fieldset/legend semantics; FieldGroup stacks fields and establishes the container query that the responsive orientation reads. Field renders a div with role="group" and data-orientation; the rest are thin wrappers over label, legend, fieldset, and p. The family holds no form state, generates no ids, and performs no validation — the label/control/error association is written by hand (htmlFor plus id, aria-invalid, data-invalid) or driven by a form library's controller.
field.whenToUse: Use for every hand-composed form field: pair FieldLabel with an Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Switch, or Slider and add FieldDescription and FieldError as needed. Use FieldSet with FieldLegend when several controls answer one question (a checkbox group, a radio group, an address block), FieldGroup to stack related fields with consistent spacing and to enable responsive orientation, and orientation="horizontal" for controls that read better beside their label such as switches and checkboxes. This is also the layer shadcn's current form guides build on — drive it with react-hook-form's Controller, TanStack Form, or Formisch.
field.whenNotToUse: Do not use Field as a general-purpose layout box: it renders role="group", which assistive technology announces, so non-form content wrapped in it is misdescribed. Do not use FieldSet and FieldLegend around a single control — the legend announces a grouping that does not exist. Do not expect Field to wire anything: if you want ids, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid applied for you inside a react-hook-form codebase, that is the older Form family (FormItem/FormControl). Do not mix the two families within one field.

values.description: Stacks label, control, description, and error in a column and stretches each to full width. The default, and the right choice for text inputs, textareas, and mobile-first layouts.

Places the label beside the control on one row. Use for switches, checkboxes, and radio items where the control is small and the label reads as a sentence. Pair with FieldContent when the field also has a description, so the description stays aligned under the label rather than stretching across the row.

Starts vertical and becomes horizontal once the surrounding FieldGroup is wide enough. It resolves against the @container/field-group container query that FieldGroup establishes, so a Field with this orientation outside a FieldGroup never switches.

orientation.description: How the label and control are arranged. Also exposed on the element as data-orientation, which FieldDescription reads to balance long helper text in horizontal layouts.

data-invalid.description: Switches the whole field block into the error treatment, including the label and description. It is styling only and is never exposed to assistive technology, so it does not replace aria-invalid on the control itself — set both. With react-hook-form this is data-invalid={fieldState.invalid}.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every control placed inside a Field
requiredAttributes.description: Give the control a stable, unique id and point the FieldLabel's htmlFor at it. Field does not generate or assign ids, so without this the control has no accessible name.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every FieldLabel
requiredAttributes.description: Must equal the id of the control the label names. This holds even in the choice-card pattern where FieldLabel wraps the whole Field: the htmlFor still targets the control's id, not the Field.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the control when the field fails validation
requiredAttributes.description: Marks the control invalid for assistive technology. Field's data-invalid only restyles the block, so aria-invalid on the control is what actually communicates the error state.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the control whenever a FieldDescription or FieldError describes it
requiredAttributes.description: The Field family does not associate helper text or errors with the control. Give the FieldDescription and FieldError elements ids and reference them from the control's aria-describedby, so the guidance is announced with the field rather than only when the FieldError alert fires.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves to the next focusable control. Field adds no keyboard behavior of its own — the wrappers are not focus stops, so tab order is exactly the order of the controls you place inside them.
Moves to the previous focusable control.

accessibility.focusManagement: Field never moves focus. FieldError renders with role="alert", so a message that appears after a failed submit is announced without stealing focus. Moving focus to the first invalid control after a failed submit is the form library's job — react-hook-form does it by default.
accessibility.notes: Clicking a FieldLabel focuses or toggles the control it names, because FieldLabel renders a real label element (Radix Label) — this only works when htmlFor matches the control's id, or when the label wraps the control. FieldSet plus FieldLegend is the only construct in the family that gives a set of controls a shared accessible name; a bare FieldGroup is a layout wrapper with no semantics. FieldTitle is styled like a label but is a plain div, so it names nothing on its own: use it only inside a choice card whose surrounding FieldLabel carries the htmlFor. Placeholder text is never a label.

subComponents.name: FieldContent
subComponents.description: A flex column that keeps the label, title, description, and error together when the control sits beside them — the layout you need for horizontal and responsive fields. Omit it in a plain vertical field with no description.

subComponents.name: FieldLabel
subComponents.description: The label for a field, rendered as a real label element (Radix Label), so clicking it focuses or toggles the control named by its htmlFor. It also accepts asChild. Beyond labeling a single control it doubles as the choice-card wrapper: wrapping a whole Field in a FieldLabel makes the entire card a click target for the radio, checkbox, or switch inside it, and the checked state restyles the card.

subComponents.name: FieldTitle
subComponents.description: Label-styled heading text for use inside FieldContent, typically as the headline of a choice card above its FieldDescription. It renders a div, not a label, so it provides no label association — the accessible name must still come from the surrounding FieldLabel or from the control.

subComponents.name: FieldDescription
subComponents.description: Helper text rendered as a p, muted and line-balanced in horizontal layouts. It may hold links. It is not automatically associated with the control: give it an id and reference it from the control's aria-describedby. It also serves as the description under a FieldLegend inside a FieldSet.

subComponents.name: FieldError
subComponents.description: The validation message container, rendered as a div with role="alert" so a message that appears after submit is announced. It takes either children or an errors array of objects with a message property — the shape react-hook-form's fieldState.error and Standard Schema issues (Zod, Valibot, ArkType) already have. Given several messages it de-duplicates them and renders a bulleted list; given nothing it renders nothing.

composition.notes: The nesting the docs prescribe is FieldSet > FieldLegend + FieldGroup > Field, and inside a Field: FieldLabel, the control, FieldDescription, FieldError — in that reading order, with FieldError immediately after the control it describes. FieldSet and FieldGroup are top-level components in this contract (they wrap Fields, they do not live inside one); upstream also allows a set-level FieldDescription, which this contract deliberately narrows to Field scope — every shipped example uses it there, and a set-level summary belongs to the legend. When the label sits beside the control, wrap the label, description, and error in FieldContent so they stay aligned. Any labelable control belongs inside a Field: Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, RadioGroupItem, Switch, Slider, InputGroup, or your own. No sub-component is marked required, deliberately: in the documented choice-card and radio patterns FieldLabel is an ancestor of Field rather than a descendant, so a structural must-contain rule would be false — the labeling requirement is carried as a constraint instead. FieldGroup is required in practice only for orientation="responsive", which resolves against the container query FieldGroup establishes.

constraints.context: A control that needs a label, helper text, and a validation message
constraints.rule: Compose Field with FieldLabel, the control, FieldDescription, and FieldError rather than hand-rolling wrapper divs

constraints.context: The association between a FieldLabel and its control
constraints.rule: Set htmlFor on the FieldLabel to the control's id — Field generates and wires nothing

constraints.context: A field that has failed validation
constraints.rule: Set aria-invalid on the control and data-invalid on the Field; data-invalid is styling only and is not announced

constraints.context: A FieldDescription or FieldError that explains a control
constraints.rule: Give it an id and reference it from the control's aria-describedby, because the family does not associate them automatically

constraints.context: Several controls that together answer one question, such as a checkbox or radio group
constraints.rule: Wrap them in a FieldSet with a FieldLegend instead of repeating a label on each control

constraints.context: A single standalone control
constraints.rule: Do not wrap it in FieldSet and FieldLegend — the legend announces a group that does not exist

constraints.context: Page or section layout of non-form content
constraints.rule: Do not use Field, FieldGroup, or FieldSet as layout boxes; Field renders role="group" and FieldSet renders a fieldset

constraints.context: A Field using orientation="responsive"
constraints.rule: Place it inside a FieldGroup, which establishes the container query the responsive orientation resolves against

constraints.context: Multiple validation messages from a schema validator
constraints.rule: Pass the issues to FieldError's errors array and let it de-duplicate and list them rather than concatenating strings

field-set.name: FieldSet
field-set.description: A semantic fieldset that groups controls answering one question — a checkbox group, a radio group, an address block. Pair it with a FieldLegend so the group has an accessible name, and put the individual Fields in a FieldGroup inside it.

subComponents.name: FieldLegend
subComponents.description: The legend element that names a FieldSet and is announced with each control inside it. Takes a variant prop of "legend" (default, section-sized) or "label" (label-sized, for nested fieldsets or when the group reads as a single field, such as a checkbox group).

field-group.name: FieldGroup
field-group.description: A layout wrapper that stacks Fields with consistent spacing and establishes the @container/field-group container query that orientation="responsive" resolves against. It carries no semantics, so it never substitutes for FieldSet. Add data-slot="checkbox-group" when it holds a checkbox group so the spacing tightens.

subComponents.name: FieldSeparator
subComponents.description: A divider between sections of a FieldGroup, optionally with inline text such as "Or continue with". Use it sparingly — every separator is a section boundary a screen reader user has to interpret.

form.name: Form
form.description: The react-hook-form wrapper family. Form is a re-export of react-hook-form's FormProvider, FormField wraps its Controller and publishes the field name on context, and FormItem generates one React id per field from which every other id is derived: the control gets `${id}-form-item`, the description `${id}-form-item-description`, the message `${id}-form-item-message`. FormControl is a Radix Slot that clones the single control inside it and stamps on id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid, so the label/description/error association is generated rather than hand-written. Form itself renders no DOM — you still write the native form element and pass form.handleSubmit(onSubmit) to its onSubmit.
form.whenToUse: Use in codebases already built on react-hook-form that want the field wiring generated: unique ids per field, htmlFor bound to the control, aria-describedby pointing at the description and, once the field errors, at the message, aria-invalid reflecting the field's error state, and the error text pulled straight out of formState without touching it.
form.whenNotToUse: Do not use without react-hook-form: every part reads context from FormProvider and FormField, so outside them useFormField throws or produces ids like "undefined-form-item". Do not use it for new work in preference to Field — shadcn still ships form in the registry, but the component no longer has a documentation page and the current form guides compose Field with Controller instead, which also gives you horizontal and responsive layouts, fieldset grouping, and support for TanStack Form and Formisch. Do not reach for it when you need a field layout the family does not have: FormItem is a plain vertical stack.

control.description: The control object returned by useForm(). In practice you never pass it alone: Form is react-hook-form's FormProvider, which takes the entire useForm() result, so the idiom is <Form {...form}>. FormField's Controller and every useFormField() consumer read the field's state through it.

formState.description: Validation and submission state from useForm(): errors, isSubmitting, isDirty, isValid. FormLabel and FormMessage reach the current field's error through it via useFormField(), which is why neither takes an error prop.

handleSubmit.description: The submit wrapper from useForm(), carried on context along with the rest of the hook result. It belongs on the native form element as onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)} — Form renders no element, so it cannot receive an onSubmit of its own.

requiredAttributes.condition: applied automatically by FormControl to the control it wraps
requiredAttributes.description: FormControl sets id to the FormItem's generated form item id. Do not set your own id on a control inside FormControl: FormLabel's htmlFor targets the generated value, and overriding it silently breaks the label association.

requiredAttributes.condition: applied automatically by FormLabel
requiredAttributes.description: FormLabel renders a Radix Label with htmlFor bound to the same generated form item id, so clicking the label focuses the control. This resolves only if the control is wrapped in FormControl and both live inside the same FormItem.

requiredAttributes.condition: applied automatically by FormControl
requiredAttributes.description: FormControl always references the FormDescription id, and appends the FormMessage id as soon as the field has an error. Render FormDescription and FormMessage inside the same FormItem, otherwise the reference points at an element that does not exist.

requiredAttributes.condition: applied automatically by FormControl when the field has an error
requiredAttributes.description: Reflects the field's error state from formState. Do not set aria-invalid by hand on a control inside FormControl — FormControl owns it and will overwrite or contradict yours depending on prop order.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the native form element when a page contains more than one form
requiredAttributes.description: Name each form so the two are distinguishable when navigating by form; reference an existing visible heading, or use aria-label when no such heading exists.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves to the next control. The Form parts add no keyboard behavior of their own — FormItem is a div and FormControl renders no element, so tab order is the order of the controls.
Moves to the previous control.
Submits the form from a single-line text control, which is native form behavior and requires a submit button in the form. It runs the resolver first, so an invalid form errors instead of submitting.

accessibility.focusManagement: On a failed submit react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field (shouldFocusError defaults to true), which works because the control keeps the ref that Controller passes through FormControl. Note that FormMessage returns null while the field is valid, so the element aria-describedby points at exists only once the field errors — and it is a plain p, not a live region, so the message is announced when the control is next read rather than at the moment it appears. If you need immediate announcement, use the Field family's FieldError, which renders with role="alert".
accessibility.notes: The family declares no ARIA role of its own: Form and FormField render nothing, FormControl renders nothing, and FormItem is a plain div — form semantics come from the native form element you write. Every part depends on both contexts: FormField supplies the field name, FormItem supplies the generated id. A FormLabel or FormControl outside a FormItem still renders, but its ids collapse to "undefined-form-item", so every such field on the page collides on the same id. A control that is not wrapped in FormControl receives no id, no aria-describedby, and no aria-invalid — the wiring is the whole point of the wrapper, and skipping it leaves an unlabeled field that looks correct on screen. FormLabel must carry visible text; a placeholder is not a label.

subComponents.name: FormField
subComponents.description: Wraps react-hook-form's Controller and publishes the field name on context so the parts beneath it can resolve their state. It takes name, control, and a render prop — the field's UI is returned from render({ field, fieldState }), not passed as children — and renders no element itself.

subComponents.name: FormItem
subComponents.description: The per-field container, a div that calls React.useId() and publishes it on context. Every id in the field derives from it, so there must be exactly one FormItem per field: two controls under one FormItem would share the same id, label, and message references.

subComponents.name: FormLabel
subComponents.description: The field's label, rendered as a Radix Label with htmlFor bound to the generated control id and data-error set when the field is invalid, which is what turns the label text destructive. It takes no error prop — it reads the field's error from context.

subComponents.name: FormControl
subComponents.description: A Radix Slot that must wrap exactly one control and renders no element of its own. It merges id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid onto that child, which is what makes the association automatic. The child must forward props and ref — every shadcn control does; a plain function component that drops them silently loses the wiring.

subComponents.name: FormDescription
subComponents.description: Helper text rendered as a p carrying the generated description id. FormControl references that id from aria-describedby unconditionally, so include a FormDescription in any FormItem where guidance helps — and know that omitting it leaves the reference pointing at nothing.

subComponents.name: FormMessage
subComponents.description: The validation message, rendered as a p carrying the generated message id. It prints the field's error message when there is one, falls back to its children when there is not, and returns null when there is neither — so the element exists only while the field is invalid. Author it in every FormItem: FormControl adds its id to aria-describedby the moment the field errors.

composition.notes: The shape is fixed: <Form {...form}> around a native <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>, then one FormField per field whose render returns a FormItem containing FormLabel, FormControl wrapping the control, an optional FormDescription, and FormMessage. Form is FormProvider and FormField is Controller, so neither emits markup — the native form element is yours to write, as are the submit Button and any layout between fields. useFormField is a hook, not a component: it is what every part calls to reach the field name, the generated ids, and the field's error. It throws outside a Form, because there is no react-hook-form context to read, and it misbehaves outside a FormField or a FormItem, where the field name and the generated id are undefined. Do not mix this family with the Field family inside one field; both want to own the association, and only one of them can.

constraints.context: A form in a codebase already built on react-hook-form
constraints.rule: Use the Form family so ids, htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid are generated instead of hand-written

constraints.context: A new form, or a form built on TanStack Form, Formisch, or no form library
constraints.rule: Compose the Field family with the library's own controller instead — shadcn's current form guides build on Field, and Form is react-hook-form-only

constraints.context: The control inside a field
constraints.rule: Wrap it in exactly one FormControl; an unwrapped control gets no id, no aria-describedby, and no aria-invalid

constraints.context: Attributes on a control inside FormControl
constraints.rule: Do not set your own id or aria-invalid — FormControl owns them and FormLabel's htmlFor targets the generated id

constraints.context: Each field rendered from a FormField's render prop
constraints.rule: Render exactly one FormItem and keep FormLabel, FormControl, FormDescription, and FormMessage inside it, so they all resolve the same generated id

constraints.context: Submitting the form
constraints.rule: Put onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)} on the native form element — Form is FormProvider and renders no DOM to receive it

constraints.context: The accessible name of each control
constraints.rule: Provide a FormLabel with visible text; a placeholder is not a label

constraints.context: A single field
constraints.rule: Do not combine Form parts with Field parts — both own the label and error association, and mixing them produces duplicate or dangling references

constraints.context: Client-side validation
constraints.rule: Define the rules once as a schema and pass it through a resolver to useForm, rather than validating inside the field components

separator.name: Separator
separator.description: A one-pixel rule that divides content. Built on Radix UI Separator. It stretches to the full width of its container when horizontal and to its full height when vertical, and it is hidden from assistive technology by default — shadcn's wrapper sets decorative to true.
separator.whenToUse: Use to mark a boundary between groups of related content: between sections of a sidebar or a settings page, between a card's header and its body, between inline metadata in a row. Reach for it when spacing alone leaves the grouping ambiguous.
separator.whenNotToUse: Do not use a Separator to create breathing room — that is what margin and padding are for. Do not use one to draw a line under a container that already has its own border. Inside a DropdownMenu, Select, or Command list, use that component's own separator part so the divider inherits the menu's spacing and semantics.

values.description: A full-width rule between stacked sections. The ordinary case.

A full-height rule between items laid out along a row — toolbars, inline stat groups, button clusters. Needs a container that resolves a height (a flex row with items-stretch, or an explicit height), or it renders as nothing.

orientation.description: The axis the rule divides across. Horizontal separates stacked content; vertical separates content sitting side by side.

decorative.description: Whether the rule is purely visual. At the default of true the element renders role="none" and assistive technology skips it entirely. Set it to false when the divider marks a real boundary — the element then renders role="separator", and a vertical one also carries aria-orientation="vertical".

requiredAttributes.condition: when the divider communicates a grouping that is not already conveyed by a heading, a landmark, or list structure
requiredAttributes.description: Pass decorative={false} so the element is exposed as role="separator" instead of role="none". shadcn defaults it to true, which removes the rule from the accessibility tree — correct for ornament, wrong for a real boundary.

requiredAttributes.condition: on a vertical separator that is not decorative
requiredAttributes.description: Emitted by the primitive from the orientation prop. Set orientation="vertical" and leave the ARIA attribute alone rather than writing it by hand.

accessibility.focusManagement: Separator is never focusable and never enters the tab order; it has no keyboard behaviour of its own.
accessibility.notes: role="separator" without a tabindex is a static separator, not a splitter — never attach drag-to-resize behaviour to it. A divider the user can move is a different control with its own value semantics; use a Resizable handle for that.

constraints.context: A boundary between groups of content that is not already conveyed by a heading, landmark, or list
constraints.rule: Pass decorative={false} so the separator is announced

constraints.context: A rule that only restates a boundary already conveyed by a heading, a Card edge, or spacing
constraints.rule: Leave decorative at its default of true so assistive technology skips it

constraints.context: A vertical separator
constraints.rule: Give it a container that resolves a height — a flex row with items-stretch, or an explicit height; a vertical separator in an auto-height parent collapses to zero pixels

constraints.context: Creating visual breathing room between elements
constraints.rule: Use spacing utilities instead of a Separator

constraints.context: Dividing items inside a DropdownMenu, Select, or Command list
constraints.rule: Use that component's own separator part instead of a standalone Separator

constraints.context: A divider the user can drag to resize the panes on either side
constraints.rule: Use a Resizable handle instead of a Separator, which is neither focusable nor operable

avatar.name: Avatar
avatar.description: A compact, rounded stand-in for a person or entity.
