Built on Radix UI Avatar: AvatarImage mounts only once the image has actually loaded, and AvatarFallback fills the same box while it is loading or whenever it is missing or broken — so the slot is never empty and the layout never shifts.
avatar.whenToUse: Use to identify a person, organisation, or account at a glance: comment authors, assignees in a table row, members in a list, the signed-in user behind a menu trigger. Use AvatarGroup when several participants have to share one slot.
avatar.whenNotToUse: Do not use Avatar for imagery that is not standing in for an identity — thumbnails, cover art, product photos belong in an AspectRatio or a plain image. Do not make the Avatar itself clickable; wrap it in a Button, a link, or a DropdownMenuTrigger so the control is focusable and named. Do not use an avatar alone to carry status.

values.description: 24px. For dense table rows, inline mentions, and compact toolbars.
32px. The standard avatar for lists, comments, and row-level identity.
40px. For profile headers and cards where the person is the subject of the surface.

size.description: Preset avatar diameter. AvatarBadge and AvatarGroupCount scale from this value, so change the size here rather than overriding the box with utility classes.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every AvatarImage
requiredAttributes.description: AvatarImage renders a native img. Name the person or entity when the avatar is the only thing identifying them; pass an empty string when their name is already visible beside it, so the identity is not announced twice. The attribute itself is never optional — a missing alt leaves the file name as the accessible name.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the Avatar is the visual for a control — inside a Button, a link, or a DropdownMenuTrigger
requiredAttributes.description: Name the control by what it does ("Open account menu"), not by the picture. The wrapping control owns the accessible name; the Avatar inside it should be decorative.

accessibility.focusManagement: Avatar is not focusable and takes no part in the tab order. When it is the visual for a control, the wrapping element owns focus and must show the focus ring — the avatar's own rounding should not clip it.
accessibility.notes: AvatarFallback is not a nicety: it is what most users on slow or blocked connections actually see, and what renders whenever the URL 404s. Give it initials or an identifying icon, never an empty box. Initials are a weak identity on their own, so keep the person's name in adjacent text or in the image's alt.

subComponents.name: AvatarImage
subComponents.description: The photograph itself, rendered as a native img from the src and alt you pass. Radix keeps it unmounted until the image has loaded successfully, so a slow or broken URL never paints a blank circle; onLoadingStatusChange reports idle, loading, loaded, or error when you need to react to that.

subComponents.name: AvatarFallback
subComponents.description: What occupies the avatar's box while the image loads and whenever it is absent or fails. Holds one or two initials, or an icon. Its delayMs prop holds the fallback back for a moment so a fast image does not flash initials first.

subComponents.name: AvatarBadge
subComponents.description: A small indicator pinned to the bottom-right of the avatar for presence or status — online, away, verified. It sizes itself from the parent Avatar's size prop. Purely visual: it exposes no accessible name of its own, so the state it signals has to exist in text too.

subComponents.name: AvatarGroup
subComponents.description: A row of overlapping Avatars representing several people in a single slot. It inverts the usual nesting — it is a wrapper around Avatar instances rather than a child of one — and applies the overlap and ring treatment to each avatar it holds.

subComponents.name: AvatarGroupCount
subComponents.description: The trailing counter that closes an AvatarGroup and stands in for the participants not shown, typically written as "+3". Matches the size of the avatars beside it and takes text or an icon.

composition.notes: An Avatar holds an AvatarImage and an AvatarFallback, optionally followed by an AvatarBadge. The fallback is the required part, not the image: an avatar with no image is ordinary, an avatar with nothing to show when the image fails is a bug. AvatarGroup sits outside this nesting — it is a parent that contains several Avatars, optionally closed by an AvatarGroupCount — so treat it as a sibling concern rather than a slot inside Avatar.

constraints.context: Every Avatar
constraints.rule: Include an AvatarFallback with initials or an identifying icon; the image may never arrive

constraints.context: An AvatarImage
constraints.rule: Always pass alt — the person's or entity's name when the avatar identifies them, an empty string when that name is already visible beside it

constraints.context: An avatar that opens a menu or navigates somewhere
constraints.rule: Wrap the Avatar in a Button, link, or DropdownMenuTrigger and name that control; do not attach the handler to the Avatar

constraints.context: Changing the avatar's diameter
constraints.rule: Use the size prop rather than overriding the box with utility classes, so AvatarBadge and AvatarGroupCount stay in proportion

constraints.context: Presence or status shown with an AvatarBadge
constraints.rule: State the status in text as well; the badge is a coloured dot with no accessible name

constraints.context: Thumbnails, cover art, product photos, or any imagery that is not an identity
constraints.rule: Use AspectRatio with an image instead of Avatar

constraints.context: More participants than fit the row
constraints.rule: Cap the visible avatars in an AvatarGroup and close it with an AvatarGroupCount instead of shrinking them all

accordion.name: Accordion
accordion.description: A stack of headings that each reveal a panel of content. Built on Radix UI Accordion. The root decides whether one section or several can be open at a time; each item pairs a trigger — a button inside a heading — with the region that trigger controls.
accordion.whenToUse: Use to compress a long page of self-contained sections into a list of headings someone can scan and open selectively: FAQs, grouped settings, order or invoice details, reference documentation. It works when the headings alone are enough to decide what to open, and when the sections are peers rather than steps.
accordion.whenNotToUse: Do not hide content the reader needs in order to act — pricing, validation errors, required form fields, or anything they must compare across sections. For a single region that shows and hides, use Collapsible; there is no heading list to justify an accordion of one. For mutually exclusive views of the same subject, use Tabs. For content that merely overflows its box, use ScrollArea. For an ordered, multi-step task, use a stepper rather than an accordion.

values.description: One section open at a time; opening one closes the last. Use when the panels are long enough that two open at once would be hard to read. Pair it with collapsible so the reader can also close everything.
Sections open and close independently and any number can be open at once. Use when the reader may want to hold several panels open together, such as a settings page or a comparison.

type.description: Whether the accordion is a one-at-a-time disclosure or a set of independent ones. Radix requires it — there is no default. It also decides the shape of value and defaultValue: a string when single, an array of strings when multiple.

collapsible.description: Only meaningful when type is "single". At the default of false one section is always open and clicking the open trigger does nothing; set it to true so the reader can collapse the last open section. It has no effect when type is "multiple", where every item can already close.

defaultValue.description: The item value or values open on first render, for an uncontrolled accordion. A string when type is "single", an array when it is "multiple". Use it to open the section that answers the reader's most likely question.

value.description: The open item value or values when you drive the accordion yourself. Pair it with onValueChange. Prefer defaultValue unless something outside the accordion has to open or close sections.

onValueChange.description: Fires with the new open value or values whenever a section opens or closes. Required for a controlled accordion, and useful on an uncontrolled one for analytics.

disabled.description: Disables every trigger in the accordion. When only one section is unavailable, set disabled on that AccordionItem instead.

values.description: Stacked headings — the ordinary arrangement. Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between triggers.

Triggers arranged along a row. Arrow Left and Arrow Right move between them. Rare: the prop sets the ARIA orientation and the arrow-key mapping, but the visual arrangement is still yours to build, and shadcn's default styles assume vertical.

orientation.description: The axis the triggers are arranged along, which decides which arrow keys navigate between them and what aria-orientation the root reports.

values.description: Left-to-right reading order.
Right-to-left reading order, which swaps the meaning of Arrow Left and Arrow Right in a horizontal accordion.

dir.description: Reading direction. Inherit it from a DirectionProvider at the root of the app rather than setting it per accordion.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every AccordionItem
requiredAttributes.description: A unique, stable string identifying the section. It is the vocabulary value, defaultValue, and onValueChange speak in, and the primitive derives the trigger and panel id wiring from it. Use meaningful slugs rather than positional indexes, so the open section survives reordering and filtering.

requiredAttributes.condition: supplied by the primitive on every trigger
requiredAttributes.description: Radix sets it from the open state, alongside aria-controls on the trigger and aria-labelledby on the panel. Do not write these by hand — overriding them desynchronises what is announced from what is visible.

keyboardInteractions.description: When focus is on a trigger, toggles that section.
When focus is on a trigger, toggles that section.
Moves focus to the next trigger in a vertical accordion.
Moves focus to the previous trigger in a vertical accordion.
Moves focus to the next trigger in a horizontal accordion.
Moves focus to the previous trigger in a horizontal accordion.
Moves focus to the first trigger.
Moves focus to the last trigger.
Moves focus to the next focusable element in the document — the first focusable child of an open panel when there is one, otherwise the next trigger.
Moves focus to the previous focusable element.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focus stays on the trigger when a section expands or collapses; the panel is never auto-focused, so the reader chooses when to enter it with Tab. Only triggers participate in arrow-key navigation. A closed panel is unmounted, so nothing inside it can hold focus — which is also why in-page anchors and browser find-in-page cannot reach it.
accessibility.notes: The accordion root carries no ARIA role of its own; the semantics live in its parts. Each AccordionTrigger is a button wrapped in Radix's Header, which renders an h3, and each AccordionContent is exposed as a region labelled by its trigger. Because that heading level is fixed at h3 in shadcn's generated component, place the accordion beneath an h2 so the document outline stays ordered. The trigger label is the only thing a screen-reader user has to decide on, so it must describe the panel, not gesture at it.

subComponents.name: AccordionItem
subComponents.description: One section: a trigger and the panel it controls. Its required value prop is the section's identity — unique within the accordion and stable across renders. Set disabled here to make a single section unavailable without disabling the whole accordion.

subComponents.name: AccordionTrigger
subComponents.description: The heading button that opens and closes its section. shadcn renders it inside Radix's Header and appends the chevron that rotates with the open state, so a text label is all it needs from you. Write the label so the reader can decide whether to open the panel from that text alone.

subComponents.name: AccordionContent
subComponents.description: The panel a trigger reveals, exposed as a region labelled by that trigger. It is unmounted while closed, so what is inside is invisible to find-in-page, to deep links, and to print. Takes prose, controls, or whole layouts.

composition.notes: An Accordion contains one or more AccordionItems and nothing else directly. Each item holds exactly one AccordionTrigger followed by one AccordionContent, in that order. The heading wrapper around the trigger is rendered for you — do not add your own heading inside AccordionTrigger, and do not nest a button, link, or form control in it, since the trigger is itself a button.

constraints.context: Every Accordion
constraints.rule: Set type explicitly — single when the panels are long and only one should be open, multiple when the sections are independent

constraints.context: An accordion with type="single"
constraints.rule: Set collapsible so the reader can close the open section; without it one section is always open

constraints.context: An accordion with type="multiple"
constraints.rule: Do not pass collapsible — it has no effect, because every item can already be closed

constraints.context: Every AccordionItem
constraints.rule: Give it a unique, stable value; positional values break as soon as items are reordered or filtered

constraints.context: The children of an AccordionItem
constraints.rule: Include exactly one AccordionTrigger followed by one AccordionContent

constraints.context: Every AccordionTrigger
constraints.rule: Give it a visible text label that says what the panel contains

constraints.context: Buttons, links, or form controls inside an AccordionTrigger
constraints.rule: Move them into the panel; the trigger is already a button and nested interactive elements are invalid and unreachable

constraints.context: Content that must be reachable by find-in-page, deep link, or print
constraints.rule: Keep it outside the accordion; closed panels are unmounted

constraints.context: A single region that shows and hides
constraints.rule: Use Collapsible instead of an accordion with one item

constraints.context: Mutually exclusive views of the same subject
constraints.rule: Use Tabs instead of a single-type Accordion

constraints.context: An accordion placed under a page or section heading
constraints.rule: Put an h2 above it so the outline stays ordered; the triggers render as h3

scroll-area.name: Scroll Area
scroll-area.description: A bounded region that scrolls with a styled scrollbar that looks the same in every browser. Built on Radix UI ScrollArea: the content sits in a native overflow viewport, so scrolling itself stays native, while the visible scrollbar is a custom element that overlays the content instead of taking width from it.
scroll-area.whenToUse: Use where a fixed-size box has to hold more content than fits and the platform scrollbar would be intrusive or inconsistent: a sidebar of navigation links, a long list inside a popover or dialog, a log or code panel, a horizontal row of cards. The bounded height or width is what makes it scroll.
scroll-area.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the page itself — the document's own scrolling carries scroll restoration, anchor navigation, browser chrome behaviour, and the scrollbar people expect. Do not use it to tuck away content you would rather not lay out: if the content matters, give it room. For very long or virtualised lists, point the virtualiser at the viewport element or use a native overflow container, since the custom scrollbar has to measure content it does not own.

values.description: Scrollbars appear while the pointer is over the area and fade out after scrolling stops. The default and the quietest — but it tells a reader nothing until they hover.
Scrollbars appear while the user is scrolling and fade out afterwards. Use when hovering should not reveal chrome, as on a dense dashboard.
Scrollbars are visible whenever the content overflows on that axis, like a traditional desktop scrollbar. Use when the fact that there is more content must always be discoverable.
Scrollbars are visible whether or not the content overflows. Use to keep the layout identical across empty, short, and long states.

type.description: When the custom scrollbars are shown. Anything other than auto or always hides the strongest signal that there is more content, so pair hover or scroll with another cue.

scrollHideDelay.description: Milliseconds to wait after scrolling stops or the pointer leaves before hiding the scrollbars. Applies only when type is "hover" or "scroll".

values.description: Left-to-right: the vertical scrollbar sits on the right and horizontal content starts at the left edge.
Right-to-left: the vertical scrollbar moves to the left and horizontal scrolling starts from the right edge.

dir.description: Reading direction, which decides which side the vertical scrollbar sits on and where horizontal scrolling begins. Inherit it from a DirectionProvider where you can.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the scroll area holds a distinct body of content — a log, a list, a panel of links — and no visible heading names it
requiredAttributes.description: Props you pass to ScrollArea land on its root element, so name the region there and pair the name with role="region". Without a name, a keyboard user who lands in the scroller is told only that they are in a group.

requiredAttributes.condition: when a visible heading already names the region
requiredAttributes.description: Reference that heading's id instead of repeating the name in aria-label. Use one or the other, never both.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the scrollable content contains no focusable elements of its own and you must support browsers that do not focus scroll containers
requiredAttributes.description: Chrome 127+ and Firefox let the keyboard focus a scroll container with no focusable children — which is why shadcn styles a focus ring on the viewport. Where you cannot rely on that, the viewport needs an explicit tabIndex={0}, and setting it means editing the generated component: props passed to ScrollArea go to the root, not to the viewport that actually scrolls.

keyboardInteractions.description: Scrolls the viewport by a line when the scroll container has focus. Handled natively by the browser — Radix adds no key handling of its own.
Scrolls by roughly one viewport height when the scroll container has focus.
Jumps to the start or the end of the scrollable content when the scroll container has focus.
Moves focus through focusable content inside the viewport; the browser scrolls each newly focused element into view.

accessibility.focusManagement: The scrollbar and its thumb are pointer-only affordances: they take no focus and answer no keys, so they must never be the only way to reach content. Keyboard scrolling comes from the browser acting on the focused element's scroll container — either something inside the viewport holds focus, or the viewport itself does.
accessibility.notes: Radix deliberately leaves the viewport, scrollbar, thumb, and corner without ARIA roles: the scrolling is native and the bar is decoration over it. That also means an overflowing ScrollArea offers no built-in hint that content continues, so keep an edge fade, a count, or a heading nearby. Never suppress native scrolling in favour of the custom bar.

subComponents.name: ScrollBar
subComponents.description: The visible scrollbar track for one axis, exported alongside ScrollArea. A vertical one is rendered inside every ScrollArea for you; add a second as a direct child with orientation="horizontal" when the content scrolls sideways. It renders its own thumb and takes no children.

subComponents.name: ScrollAreaThumb
subComponents.description: The draggable indicator inside a scrollbar, sized from the ratio of visible to total content. Every ScrollBar renders one automatically; it is not exported from the generated component and is never authored by hand. Pointer-only — it takes no focus and answers no keys.

composition.notes: ScrollArea puts whatever you give it inside Radix's Viewport — the element that actually scrolls — and renders a vertical ScrollBar and a Corner beside it. Neither the viewport nor the corner is exported, so the only part you write yourself is an extra ScrollBar with orientation="horizontal". Size comes from the ScrollArea itself: with no bounded box there is no overflow and nothing scrolls.

constraints.context: Every ScrollArea
constraints.rule: Constrain its box — a height for vertical scrolling, a width for horizontal; an area free to grow never overflows and never scrolls

constraints.context: Content that scrolls horizontally
constraints.rule: Add a ScrollBar with orientation="horizontal" as a child of the ScrollArea; only the vertical one is rendered for you

constraints.context: A scrollable region whose content holds no focusable elements
constraints.rule: Make the region keyboard focusable and give it an accessible name, so its content is reachable without a pointer

constraints.context: The page's main scroll
constraints.rule: Use the document's own scrolling instead of wrapping the page in a ScrollArea

constraints.context: A hover or scroll type where noticing the extra content matters
constraints.rule: Use type="auto", or pair it with another cue such as an edge fade or a visible boundary

constraints.context: Very long or virtualised lists
constraints.rule: Point the virtualiser at the viewport element, or use a native overflow container instead

constraints.context: A ScrollArea nested inside another ScrollArea
constraints.rule: Restructure so only one region scrolls; nested scroll chains fight over the same wheel and touch gestures

constraints.context: The ScrollBar and its thumb
constraints.rule: Do not treat them as controls or hang behaviour on them; they are pointer-only decoration over native scrolling

aspect-ratio.name: Aspect Ratio
aspect-ratio.description: A box that holds a fixed width-to-height ratio at any width. Built on Radix UI AspectRatio, which reserves the space up front rather than waiting for the content, so an image, video, or map keeps its slot from the first paint and nothing below it jumps when the asset arrives.
aspect-ratio.whenToUse: Use to reserve space for media whose intrinsic size you do not control or do not yet know: remote images, video and map embeds, iframes, and the skeletons that stand in for them. Use it across a grid or list so every tile crops to the same shape.
aspect-ratio.whenNotToUse: Do not wrap text or anything that has to grow with its content — a fixed ratio clips or stretches it. Do not use it for media whose intrinsic dimensions are known and stable; set width and height on the element and let the browser reserve the space. For a plain fixed ratio in a modern browser, the CSS aspect-ratio utility (Tailwind's aspect-video, aspect-square) does the same job without a wrapper element.

ratio.description: Width divided by height. Write it as a division — 16 / 9 for video, 4 / 3 for classic photography, 1 for a square, 9 / 16 for portrait — so the intent survives review. Left unset the box is square, which is rarely what the design meant.

accessibility.notes: AspectRatio is a presentational box: it renders no ARIA role and contributes nothing to the accessibility tree. The content inside keeps its own obligations — an img still needs alt, an iframe still needs a title, a video still needs captions. Because content is usually fitted with object-cover, check that the crop never removes information the reader needs, such as text baked into an image; where it would, use object-contain and accept the letterboxing.

constraints.context: Every AspectRatio
constraints.rule: Set ratio explicitly rather than relying on the 1:1 default

constraints.context: Media placed inside an AspectRatio
constraints.rule: Make it fill the box — full height and width with object-cover, or object-contain where cropping would lose meaning; otherwise the reserved space and the media disagree

constraints.context: Text or any content that must grow with its length
constraints.rule: Lay it out normally instead of wrapping it in an AspectRatio, which clips at the fixed ratio

constraints.context: Media with known, stable intrinsic dimensions
constraints.rule: Set width and height on the element and let the browser reserve the space, instead of adding an AspectRatio wrapper

constraints.context: A single fixed ratio in a browser that supports the CSS aspect-ratio property
constraints.rule: Use the aspect-video or aspect-square utility instead of an AspectRatio wrapper

constraints.context: An iframe or video embed inside an AspectRatio
constraints.rule: Keep the embed's own accessible name — a title on the iframe — since AspectRatio supplies none

constraints.context: An image inside an AspectRatio
constraints.rule: Give it alt text; the wrapper is invisible to assistive technology

tabs.name: Tabs
tabs.description: A set of layered content panels where only one is visible at a time, selected by a trigger in a tablist. Built on Radix UI Tabs: the root generates the ids that pair each trigger with its panel, wires aria-controls and aria-labelledby between them, applies a roving tabindex across the tablist, and reflects the selection with data-state="active". shadcn adds styling, plus a variant prop on TabsList.
tabs.whenToUse: Use when one subject has several peer views that a user switches between and rarely needs side by side: sections of a settings page, an entity's Overview / Activity / Members, a code-and-preview toggle. Tabs suit a small, stable set of short labels that fit on one line, over panels whose content is already loaded or cheap to fetch.
tabs.whenNotToUse: Do not use Tabs to move between routes or pages. A tablist is a widget, not site navigation: use links, NavigationMenu, or a sidebar so history, the back button, and open-in-new-tab keep working. Do not use Tabs for ordered steps in a flow (use a stepper) or for content the reader must compare or read together (lay it out together). When labels wrap, when the set outgrows a single row, or when panels hold long-form prose, prefer Accordion, a Select, or in-page navigation.

value.description: The value of the selected tab in controlled mode. While this is set the component never changes panels on its own; the app must respond to onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: The tab selected on first render in uncontrolled mode. Supply this or value: with neither, nothing is selected and every panel stays hidden.

onValueChange.description: Called with the newly selected tab's value whenever the selection changes. Required alongside value in controlled mode.

values.description: Triggers sit in a row above their panels and Left/Right arrows move between them. The default, and the right choice for most tab sets.
Triggers stack in a column beside the panel, Up/Down arrows move between them, and the tablist is exposed with aria-orientation="vertical". Use for a side rail of sections next to a wide panel.

orientation.description: Layout axis of the tablist. This also decides which arrow keys traverse the triggers, so it must match how the triggers are actually laid out.

values.description: Left-to-right: Arrow Right advances to the next trigger.
Right-to-left: Arrow Left advances to the next trigger.

dir.description: Reading direction of the tablist, which determines which arrow key advances. Inherited from an ancestor Radix DirectionProvider when omitted; set it explicitly only when this tab set reads in a different direction from the page.

values.description: Moving focus with the arrow keys selects that tab immediately. Correct whenever panels appear without noticeable latency; this is the behavior the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern recommends.

Arrow keys move focus without changing the panel, and the user presses Enter or Space to select. Use when selecting a tab is expensive, such as a fetch or a heavy mount, so traversing the tablist does not fire one request per tab.

activationMode.description: Whether arrow-key focus also selects. Switch to manual only when automatic selection would be slow enough to punish keyboard traversal.

asChild.description: Merges the root's props onto its single child element instead of rendering a div. Rarely needed; the root carries no semantics of its own.

requiredAttributes.condition: on TabsList when no visible heading names the tab set
requiredAttributes.description: Name the tablist so its purpose is announced when a screen reader user reaches it. Name what the tabs are for; the tablist role is already announced, so do not repeat the word "tabs".

requiredAttributes.condition: on TabsList when a visible heading already names the tab set
requiredAttributes.description: Reference the id of that heading rather than duplicating its text in aria-label. Use one or the other, never both.

requiredAttributes.condition: on a TabsTrigger whose content is an icon with no visible text
requiredAttributes.description: Give the trigger a text name. An icon-only trigger is otherwise announced as an unnamed tab.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves focus into the tablist, landing on the selected trigger: the whole tablist is one tab stop, not one per tab. From the selected trigger, Tab moves into the active panel, which Radix makes focusable so panels holding no controls of their own are still reachable.
Moves focus to the next trigger in a horizontal tablist (the previous one when dir is rtl), wrapping at the end while TabsList loop is true. In automatic activation mode the panel changes with focus.
Moves focus to the previous trigger in a horizontal tablist (the next one when dir is rtl), wrapping at the start while TabsList loop is true.
Moves focus to the next trigger in a vertical tablist, wrapping at the end while TabsList loop is true.
Moves focus to the previous trigger in a vertical tablist, wrapping at the start while TabsList loop is true.
Moves focus to the first trigger in the tablist.
Moves focus to the last trigger in the tablist.
Selects the focused trigger. Only meaningful when activationMode is manual; under automatic activation the tab is already selected.
Selects the focused trigger. Only meaningful when activationMode is manual; under automatic activation the tab is already selected.

accessibility.focusManagement: The tablist is a single tab stop with roving tabindex: only the selected trigger is reachable with Tab, and arrow keys move focus among the others. Triggers marked disabled are skipped by arrow traversal. Radix gives the active TabsContent tabindex="0", so Tab from the selected trigger lands inside the panel even when the panel contains nothing focusable, and Shift+Tab from the panel returns to the selected trigger. The selection lives in component state and not in the URL, so a reload or a shared link returns to defaultValue unless the app lifts the value into routing state.
accessibility.notes: Radix generates the id, aria-controls, and aria-labelledby pairing between each trigger and its panel from the shared value; do not hand-author or override those attributes. Unselected panels are unmounted (or, with forceMount, present but hidden), so their content is absent from the accessibility tree, from in-page find, and from print output. Content that must be findable, printable, or comparable does not belong behind a tab.

subComponents.name: TabsList
subComponents.description: The tablist: the single-tab-stop container that holds the triggers. Renders Radix Tabs.List with role="tablist" and aria-orientation taken from the root's orientation, and carries the accessible name for the tab set.

values.description: A filled, segmented control on a muted background. Use inside cards and panels where the tab set needs a contained shape.
Transparent triggers with an underline marking the selection. Use at the top of a page or section where a filled control would read as too heavy.

variant.description: Visual treatment of the tablist, applied to the triggers through a data attribute.

loop.description: Whether arrow-key focus wraps from the last trigger to the first and back. Leave it on unless the ends of the tablist must feel like hard stops.

asChild.description: Merges the tablist's props and role onto its single child element instead of rendering a div.

subComponents.name: TabsTrigger
subComponents.description: One tab. Renders a real button with role="tab", aria-selected, and aria-controls pointing at the panel whose value matches its own. The value prop is the join key with TabsContent.

value.description: Identifies this tab and joins it to the TabsContent carrying the same value. Must be unique within the tab set.

disabled.description: Makes the tab unselectable and removes it from arrow-key traversal. Prefer omitting a tab entirely over showing a permanently disabled one; a disabled tab with no explanation is a dead end.

asChild.description: Merges the trigger's props, role, and behavior onto its single child element instead of rendering a button. The child must still be a control that can receive focus.

subComponents.name: TabsContent
subComponents.description: The panel belonging to one tab. Renders with role="tabpanel" and aria-labelledby pointing back at its trigger, and is mounted only while its value is selected unless forceMount is set.

value.description: Joins this panel to the TabsTrigger carrying the same value. A panel whose value matches no trigger never renders.

forceMount.description: Keeps the panel mounted while it is hidden instead of unmounting it on switch. Use it to preserve state that would otherwise be lost, such as a partly filled form or a scroll position, or to hand an animation library control of the exit.

asChild.description: Merges the panel's props and role onto its single child element instead of rendering a div.

composition.notes: TabsContent is a sibling of TabsList inside the root, never a child of it: the tablist holds only triggers. Every TabsTrigger value must match exactly one TabsContent value, and vice versa; an unmatched trigger selects nothing and an unmatched panel never appears. Keep the DOM order of the panels aligned with the order of their triggers so tab order and reading order agree.

constraints.context: One subject with several peer views the user switches between
constraints.rule: Use Tabs

constraints.context: Moving between routes, pages, or views the user should be able to link to, bookmark, or reach with the back button
constraints.rule: Use links or NavigationMenu instead of Tabs

constraints.context: Any Tabs root
constraints.rule: Supply defaultValue, or value together with onValueChange; with neither, no tab is selected and every panel is hidden

constraints.context: Every TabsTrigger and TabsContent pair
constraints.rule: Give them the same value, unique within the tab set, so the trigger's aria-controls resolves to a real panel

constraints.context: The tab set has no visible heading that names it
constraints.rule: Give TabsList an accessible name with aria-label, or point aria-labelledby at the heading that names it

constraints.context: Selecting a tab starts a network request or mounts an expensive view
constraints.rule: Set activationMode="manual" so arrow-key traversal does not fire one request per tab

constraints.context: Content that must be reachable by in-page search, printable, or comparable side by side
constraints.rule: Do not place it in a tab panel; unselected panels are unmounted, and forceMount only keeps them hidden

constraints.context: Panel state that must survive switching away and back, such as a partly filled form
constraints.rule: Set forceMount on that TabsContent so the panel stays mounted while hidden

constraints.context: Ordered steps in a flow the user works through once
constraints.rule: Use a stepper or wizard rather than Tabs

constraints.context: A Tabs root placed inside another Tabs panel
constraints.rule: Avoid a second level of tabs; restructure the page or use an Accordion inside the panel

constraints.context: The tablist is laid out vertically
constraints.rule: Set orientation="vertical" so arrow-key traversal and aria-orientation match what is on screen

breadcrumb.name: Breadcrumb
breadcrumb.description: A trail of links showing where the current page sits in a hierarchy, ending in the current page itself. Renders a nav landmark labelled "breadcrumb" around an ordered list: ancestors are BreadcrumbLink anchors, the final crumb is a BreadcrumbPage, and decorative BreadcrumbSeparator items sit between them. The trail is authored by hand; the component does not read the router or derive itself from the URL.
breadcrumb.whenToUse: Use on pages two or more levels deep in a hierarchy the user can actually navigate up: documentation sections, category to subcategory to product, workspace to project to resource. A breadcrumb answers "where am I" and offers one-click ascent to any ancestor, which is most valuable on detail views people arrive at from search or a deep link.
breadcrumb.whenNotToUse: Do not use a breadcrumb as a site's primary navigation, and do not use one on a flat site or a single-level hierarchy where a "Back to X" link says the same thing with less furniture. Do not use it to show where the user has been; a breadcrumb reflects the structure of the site, not the path the user took. Do not use it for progress through a multi-step flow (use a stepper) or for switching between peer views (use Tabs).

aria-label.description: The accessible name of the nav landmark, preset to "breadcrumb". Override it only to localize the label or to distinguish this trail when the page carries more than one navigation landmark.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every BreadcrumbLink
requiredAttributes.description: BreadcrumbLink renders a bare anchor. Without href it is neither focusable nor announced as a link, so a click handler on it is unreachable from the keyboard. Give it the ancestor's URL, or set asChild and pass a router link that renders one.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the crumb representing the current page
requiredAttributes.description: Supplied automatically by BreadcrumbPage as aria-current="page", alongside role="link" and aria-disabled="true". Exactly one crumb carries it and it is the last one; never add aria-current to the ancestor links.

requiredAttributes.condition: when BreadcrumbEllipsis is used as the visible content of a trigger, such as a DropdownMenuTrigger
requiredAttributes.description: The ellipsis is aria-hidden and contributes no accessible name, so the trigger would otherwise be announced as unnamed. Give the trigger its own name with aria-label or a visually hidden span; shadcn's example uses a span reading "Toggle menu".

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves to the next crumb link. Every link is its own tab stop: a breadcrumb has no roving focus and no arrow-key navigation, because it is a list of links rather than a composite widget.
Follows the focused crumb link. Space does not activate an anchor; that is native link behavior, not a gap in the component.

accessibility.focusManagement: Nothing is trapped or moved: focus follows document order through the crumb links. BreadcrumbPage is deliberately not focusable, because the current page is not a destination. When collapsed crumbs are opened from a DropdownMenu, that menu owns focus while open and returns it to its trigger on close.
accessibility.notes: BreadcrumbList is an ordered list because the order of the crumbs carries meaning; never reorder crumbs for visual balance and never let a separator carry meaning, since separators are role="presentation" and aria-hidden="true". BreadcrumbPage renders a span with role="link" and aria-disabled="true" rather than an anchor, so the current page is announced in the trail without inviting a navigation that goes nowhere. BreadcrumbEllipsis is aria-hidden in its entirety, so the visually hidden "More" text inside it is never announced; treat the glyph as decoration and put the real affordance on the control that wraps it.

subComponents.name: BreadcrumbList
subComponents.description: The ordered list (ol) holding the trail. Wraps onto more than one line when the trail is long, so a wrapping trail is a signal to collapse rather than to shrink the type.

subComponents.name: BreadcrumbItem
subComponents.description: One entry in the trail, rendered as an li. Holds a BreadcrumbLink, a BreadcrumbPage, or a collapse control such as a DropdownMenu wrapping BreadcrumbEllipsis.

subComponents.name: BreadcrumbLink
subComponents.description: A link to an ancestor. Renders an anchor by default; set asChild to hand rendering to a routing library's link component so client-side navigation is preserved.

href.description: The ancestor's URL. Required for the crumb to be focusable and announced as a link, unless asChild is set and the child supplies its own destination.

asChild.description: Renders the link's props and styling onto its single child instead of an anchor, so a router link such as Next.js Link or React Router Link can take over navigation.

subComponents.name: BreadcrumbPage
subComponents.description: The final crumb: the page the user is on. Renders a span carrying role="link", aria-disabled="true", and aria-current="page", and is deliberately not a link. Exactly one per trail, always last.

subComponents.name: BreadcrumbSeparator
subComponents.description: The divider between crumbs, rendered as an li with role="presentation" and aria-hidden="true". Defaults to a chevron; pass children to substitute another glyph such as a slash.

subComponents.name: BreadcrumbEllipsis
subComponents.description: The collapsed-crumbs indicator: an aria-hidden span holding a horizontal-ellipsis icon. It is decoration and is not focusable, so wrap it in a DropdownMenu or Drawer trigger that carries its own accessible name to make the hidden ancestors reachable.

composition.notes: Breadcrumb takes exactly one BreadcrumbList, and every crumb and separator is an li inside it: nothing may sit between the ol and its li children. Order the crumbs root first and end with a single BreadcrumbPage. When the trail outgrows its container, replace the middle crumbs with one BreadcrumbEllipsis inside a DropdownMenu rather than truncating labels, keeping the root and the current page visible.

constraints.context: A page two or more levels deep in a navigable hierarchy
constraints.rule: Use Breadcrumb to show the path and offer one-click ascent to each ancestor

constraints.context: The last crumb, representing the page being viewed
constraints.rule: Use BreadcrumbPage rather than BreadcrumbLink; the current page must not link to itself

constraints.context: Any breadcrumb trail
constraints.rule: Include exactly one BreadcrumbPage, as the final item, so exactly one crumb carries aria-current="page"

constraints.context: Every BreadcrumbLink
constraints.rule: Give it an href, or set asChild and pass a link that renders one; an anchor without href is not focusable and is not announced as a link

constraints.context: An app using client-side routing
constraints.rule: Set asChild on BreadcrumbLink and pass the router's link component instead of a bare anchor, so ascending the trail does not force a full page load

constraints.context: The visual divider between crumbs
constraints.rule: Do not put meaning in BreadcrumbSeparator; it is aria-hidden and never announced

constraints.context: A trail too long for its container
constraints.rule: Collapse the middle crumbs behind a BreadcrumbEllipsis inside a DropdownMenu, keeping the root and the current page visible

constraints.context: Reaching the ancestors hidden behind a collapsed trail
constraints.rule: Do not treat BreadcrumbEllipsis as the affordance; it is aria-hidden and not focusable, so wrap it in a real trigger that carries its own accessible name

constraints.context: Showing the sequence of pages the user visited
constraints.rule: Do not use Breadcrumb; it reflects site structure, not browsing history

constraints.context: Progress through a multi-step flow
constraints.rule: Use a stepper instead of Breadcrumb

constraints.context: A site with a flat structure or a single level above the current page
constraints.rule: Prefer a single "Back to X" link over a breadcrumb

pagination.name: Pagination
pagination.description: Page-by-page navigation for a paged collection: previous and next controls, numbered page links, and an ellipsis marking the pages skipped between them. Renders a nav landmark labelled "pagination" around an unordered list. The links are anchors styled with buttonVariants, and the component holds no state: the current page, the page count, and each page's href are supplied by the app.
pagination.whenToUse: Use when a collection is served in discrete, addressable pages and the user benefits from jumping directly to one: search results, a table of records, an archive. Numbered links earn their space when a page can be linked to, bookmarked, and returned to with the back button, and when knowing how many pages exist is itself useful information.
pagination.whenNotToUse: Do not use Pagination for a feed that is read continuously; infinite scroll or a "Load more" button fits that reading pattern better. Do not render numbered links over a cursor-based API that cannot address page N, since the numbers would point nowhere. Do not use it to switch between unrelated views (that is Tabs) or to step through a wizard (that is a stepper).

aria-label.description: The accessible name of the nav landmark, preset to "pagination". Override it to localize the label, or to tell two pagers apart when a page has controls both above and below a table.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every PaginationLink, PaginationPrevious, and PaginationNext
requiredAttributes.description: These render bare anchors. Without href they are not focusable and not announced as links, so a click handler attached to them cannot be reached from the keyboard. Give each the URL of the page it targets.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the link for the page currently being viewed
requiredAttributes.description: Set isActive on that PaginationLink; it applies aria-current="page" along with a data-active attribute and the outline styling. Exactly one link in a pager may carry it.

requiredAttributes.condition: on PaginationPrevious at the first page, or PaginationNext at the last
requiredAttributes.description: An anchor cannot be disabled. Drop the href and set aria-disabled="true" (removing pointer events in styling), or render a disabled Button in that item, so the control is announced as unavailable instead of leading nowhere.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the page contains more than one pagination landmark
requiredAttributes.description: Override the nav's aria-label on each pager so the two landmarks can be told apart in a screen reader's landmark list.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves to the next control in the pager. Every link is its own tab stop: the pager has no roving focus and no arrow-key navigation, because it is a list of links rather than a composite widget.
Follows the focused link. Space does not activate an anchor; that is native link behavior, not a gap in the component.

accessibility.focusManagement: The component moves no focus of its own. When a page change re-renders the results in place rather than navigating, focus is dropped to the document: send it to the results region or its heading and announce the change, or keyboard and screen reader users are left with no signal that anything happened. A real navigation to a new URL needs none of this. Keep the pager's DOM position stable across page changes so the tab order does not shift under the user.
accessibility.notes: PaginationPrevious and PaginationNext ship with aria-label values of "Go to previous page" and "Go to next page" because their visible text is hidden below the sm breakpoint, leaving an icon alone on small screens; localize those labels rather than removing them. PaginationEllipsis is aria-hidden in its entirety, so the visually hidden "More pages" text inside it is never announced. Let each numbered link's text be the page number so its accessible name distinguishes it from its neighbors.

subComponents.name: PaginationContent
subComponents.description: The unordered list (ul) that holds the pager's items, laid out in a row.

subComponents.name: PaginationItem
subComponents.description: One entry in the pager, rendered as an li. Every control belongs in one, including the ellipsis, because only li elements may be children of the ul.

subComponents.name: PaginationLink
subComponents.description: A link to a specific page. Renders an anchor styled with buttonVariants, outline while active and ghost otherwise, and applies aria-current="page" when isActive is set.

href.description: The URL of the page this link targets. Required for the control to be focusable and announced as a link.

isActive.description: Marks this link as the page currently being viewed. Applies aria-current="page" and switches the styling from ghost to outline. Exactly one link in a pager may set it.

values.description: Square, sized for a single page number. The default, and what numbered links use.
Standard button width for a link with a text label. What PaginationPrevious and PaginationNext use.
Compact height for a pager sitting inside a dense toolbar or table footer.
Large height for a pager that needs a bigger touch target.

size.description: Button size token passed through to buttonVariants. Keep one size across every control in a pager so the row stays on a single baseline.

subComponents.name: PaginationPrevious
subComponents.description: The link to the preceding page: a PaginationLink preset to size="default" with a left chevron, the label "Previous" (hidden below the sm breakpoint), and aria-label="Go to previous page". Its content is fixed, so customization happens through props rather than children.

href.description: The URL of the preceding page. Omit it, and set aria-disabled="true", when the user is already on the first page.

aria-label.description: The control's accessible name, which carries the whole meaning on small screens where the visible "Previous" text is hidden. Override it to localize, never to remove it.

subComponents.name: PaginationNext
subComponents.description: The link to the following page: a PaginationLink preset to size="default" with a right chevron, the label "Next" (hidden below the sm breakpoint), and aria-label="Go to next page". Its content is fixed, so customization happens through props rather than children.

href.description: The URL of the following page. Omit it, and set aria-disabled="true", when the user is already on the last page.

aria-label.description: The control's accessible name, which carries the whole meaning on small screens where the visible "Next" text is hidden. Override it to localize, never to remove it.

subComponents.name: PaginationEllipsis
subComponents.description: The gap marker standing in for the pages between two non-consecutive numbers. Renders an aria-hidden span holding a horizontal-ellipsis icon; it is decoration, is not focusable, and is never announced.

composition.notes: Pagination takes exactly one PaginationContent, and every control sits in its own PaginationItem because PaginationContent is a ul. Order the items as previous, then the page links with any ellipses between them, then next, and keep the set of visible numbers stable in size as the user moves through the range so the controls do not shift under the pointer.

constraints.context: A collection served in addressable pages the user may want to jump into, bookmark, or share
constraints.rule: Use Pagination with a real href for every page

constraints.context: Every PaginationLink, PaginationPrevious, and PaginationNext
constraints.rule: Give it an href; an anchor without one is not focusable and its click handler is unreachable from the keyboard

constraints.context: Client-side pagination with no URL per page
constraints.rule: Encode the page in the URL, a query parameter is enough, rather than wiring onClick to an anchor with no href; where a page genuinely cannot be addressed, render Buttons in the items instead of PaginationLink

constraints.context: The link for the page currently being viewed
constraints.rule: Mark exactly one link isActive so exactly one control carries aria-current="page"

constraints.context: Previous on the first page, or Next on the last
constraints.rule: Do not leave a live link that goes nowhere; drop the href and set aria-disabled="true", or render a disabled Button in that item

constraints.context: Direct children of PaginationContent
constraints.rule: Wrap every control, including PaginationEllipsis, in a PaginationItem, because PaginationContent renders a ul

constraints.context: A pager repeated above and below the same collection
constraints.rule: Give each nav a distinct aria-label so the two landmarks can be told apart

constraints.context: A run of pages omitted between two visible numbers
constraints.rule: Mark the gap with PaginationEllipsis rather than letting the numbers jump silently

constraints.context: Reaching the pages hidden behind an ellipsis
constraints.rule: Do not treat PaginationEllipsis as the affordance; it is aria-hidden and not focusable, so provide a real control such as a page input or a menu

constraints.context: A page change that re-renders results in place without navigating
constraints.rule: Move focus to the results region and announce the change, so keyboard and screen reader users know the content updated

constraints.context: A feed that is read continuously rather than jumped through
constraints.rule: Use infinite scroll or a "Load more" button instead of Pagination

constraints.context: A cursor-based API that cannot address an arbitrary page
constraints.rule: Do not render numbered links; expose only Previous and Next

label.name: Label
label.description: A caption that names a form control, built on Radix UI Label. Renders a native label element and suppresses text selection on double click so repeated clicks toggle the control rather than selecting its text. The label supplies the control's accessible name and extends its hit target.
label.whenToUse: Use to name every form control on a surface: Input, Textarea, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroupItem, and the Select trigger. Point htmlFor at the control's id so clicking or tapping the label focuses the control and, for checkboxes, switches, and radio items, activates it.
label.whenNotToUse: Do not use it as a general text style for headings, hint text, or table column titles — it carries labelling semantics that assistive technology will try to associate with a control. Do not use one Label to name a group of controls such as a RadioGroup or a set of related checkboxes; a fieldset with a legend names a group. Do not put one on a Button — a button's own text is its accessible name.

htmlFor.description: The id of the form control this label names. Must match that control's id exactly and that id must be unique on the page. Required unless the control is rendered inside the Label.

asChild.description: When true, merges the label's props and behavior onto its single child element instead of rendering a label element. Use only when the child is itself a labelling element; otherwise the association is lost.

requiredAttributes.condition: whenever the labelled control is not a descendant of the Label
requiredAttributes.description: Reference the control's id. This is what makes the label text the control's accessible name and makes the label a click target for it.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the control being labelled
requiredAttributes.description: The control needs a unique id for htmlFor to point at. For Select this is the id of the SelectTrigger, not of the hidden native select.

accessibility.focusManagement: Not focusable and not in the tab order. Activating the label moves focus to the associated control and, for Checkbox, Switch, and RadioGroupItem, toggles or selects it.
accessibility.notes: A label element exposes no ARIA role of its own; it contributes the accessible name of the control it references. It must contain non-empty text — an empty Label silently leaves the control unnamed. A placeholder, a title attribute, or adjacent prose that is not bound with htmlFor is not a substitute. Do not nest interactive content (buttons, links) inside a Label: clicking it would activate both the label's control and the nested control.

constraints.context: Any Input, Textarea, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroupItem, or Select on a surface
constraints.rule: Give it a Label whose htmlFor matches the control's id

constraints.context: A control whose purpose is already suggested by placeholder text
constraints.rule: Still render a Label — placeholder text disappears on input and is not an accessible name

constraints.context: Naming a group of related controls such as a RadioGroup or a set of checkboxes
constraints.rule: Use a fieldset with a legend (or aria-labelledby on the group) instead of a single Label

constraints.context: Styling non-label text such as headings, hints, or column titles
constraints.rule: Use a text element instead of Label

constraints.context: A Label that wraps the control it names
constraints.rule: Still pair an explicit htmlFor with the control's id so the association survives layout refactors

constraints.context: Interactive content such as a Button or link inside label text
constraints.rule: Move it outside the Label — activating the label would trigger both it and the labelled control

textarea.name: Textarea
textarea.description: A multi-line text input rendered as a native textarea element. The shadcn wrapper applies field-sizing-content over a minimum height, so the control grows with what the user types instead of staying at a fixed row count.
textarea.whenToUse: Use for free-form prose whose length is open-ended: descriptions, comments, support ticket bodies, release notes, feedback. Reach for it whenever a plausible answer would wrap onto a second line, or whenever the user should be able to press Enter for a new paragraph.
textarea.whenNotToUse: Do not use for single-line values such as names, email addresses, amounts, or search queries, where Enter should submit rather than insert a newline; use Input. Do not use it as a code or rich-text editor — it has no formatting, syntax, or structured undo affordances. Do not use it to collect a value from a known set of options; use Select or RadioGroup.

value.description: Controlled text content. Pair with onChange; a value without a change handler renders a read-only field that appears broken to the user.

defaultValue.description: Initial text for an uncontrolled textarea. Use this when the form reads its value on submit rather than on every keystroke.

onChange.description: Native change handler fired on each edit, receiving the textarea event.

placeholder.description: Hint text shown while the field is empty. Use it for an example of the expected content, never as the field's name — it disappears as soon as the user types.

rows.description: Native attribute for the initial visible line count. shadcn's textarea sets field-sizing-content over a minimum height, so the rendered height follows the content; set a floor or ceiling with height classes rather than relying on rows.

maxLength.description: Maximum number of characters the browser will accept. Enforcement is silent — the field simply stops accepting input — so pair it with a visible count.

disabled.description: Whether the field is non-interactive. Disabled fields are skipped by the tab order and are not submitted with the form.

readOnly.description: Whether the content is visible and selectable but not editable. Unlike disabled, a read-only field stays focusable and is still submitted.

required.description: Whether the field must be filled in before the form can be submitted. Mark the requirement visibly in the Label too, not only in markup.

name.description: Form field name under which the value is submitted.

keyboardInteractions.description: Inserts a newline. It does not submit the surrounding form, so a form containing a Textarea needs an explicit submit Button.
Moves focus out of the field. It does not insert a tab character, so keyboard users are never trapped in the textarea.

requiredAttributes.description: Required so the field's Label can reference it with htmlFor. Without the pairing the field is announced as an unnamed text area.

requiredAttributes.condition: when hint text, a character count, or an error message qualifies the field
requiredAttributes.description: Reference the ids of those elements so the guidance is announced with the field rather than being visual-only.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the field has failed validation
requiredAttributes.description: Set aria-invalid so the error state is announced, and point aria-describedby at the message that explains how to fix it. shadcn styles the invalid state from this attribute.

accessibility.notes: The field grows as the user types, so avoid absolutely positioned siblings that assume a fixed height. Character counters must be referenced with aria-describedby to be announced; a live-updating counter should not be an aria-live region on every keystroke.

constraints.context: A single-line value such as a name, email address, or search query
constraints.rule: Use Input instead of Textarea

constraints.context: Any Textarea
constraints.rule: Give it a visible Label associated by id and htmlFor

constraints.context: A field that has failed validation
constraints.rule: Set aria-invalid and reference the error message with aria-describedby

constraints.context: A field with a character limit
constraints.rule: Show the limit and the remaining count in text referenced by aria-describedby rather than relying on maxLength to cut input off silently

constraints.context: A textarea that needs a fixed or capped height
constraints.rule: Constrain it with height classes — field-sizing-content supersedes the rows attribute

constraints.context: Rich text, markdown with live preview, or code entry
constraints.rule: Use a dedicated editor instead of Textarea

checkbox.name: Checkbox
checkbox.description: A tri-state checkbox built on Radix UI Checkbox. Renders a button with role checkbox plus a visually hidden native input so the value participates in form submission. The check mark is rendered internally by the component's indicator, so there is nothing to compose inside it — the option's text belongs in a sibling Label.
checkbox.whenToUse: Use for independent boolean choices the user opts into: accepting terms, selecting rows, enabling several non-exclusive filters or permissions. Use a set of checkboxes whenever more than one option in a group may be chosen at once.
checkbox.whenNotToUse: Do not use for mutually exclusive options; use RadioGroup. Do not use for a setting that takes effect the instant it is flipped with no Save step; that is Switch. Do not use a checkbox as a trigger for an action or for navigation; use Button.

values.description: Checked. The hidden input submits the checkbox's value with the form.
Unchecked. Nothing is submitted for this field.

Mixed state for a parent checkbox whose children are only partly selected. Radix exposes it as aria-checked="mixed"; activating it resolves to checked, so it is never part of the user-facing click cycle.

checked.description: Controlled checked state. Pair it with onCheckedChange — a checked value without a handler produces a box the user cannot toggle.

defaultChecked.description: Initial state for an uncontrolled checkbox. Use this when the surrounding form reads values on submit rather than tracking them per keystroke.

onCheckedChange.description: Fires with the new state (true, false, or "indeterminate") whenever the user toggles the checkbox.

disabled.description: Whether the checkbox is non-interactive. Disabled checkboxes leave the tab order and are not submitted; if the reason is not obvious from context, explain it in nearby text.

required.description: Whether the box must be checked before the form can be submitted. Use it for consent gates, and mark the requirement visibly in the Label as well.

name.description: Form field name applied to the hidden native input, under which the value is submitted.

value.description: Value submitted when the box is checked. Set it when a group of checkboxes shares one name and the server distinguishes them by value.

keyboardInteractions.description: Toggles the checkbox.
Does not toggle the checkbox. Radix suppresses Enter to match native checkbox behavior.
Moves focus to the checkbox. Every checkbox is its own tab stop — unlike RadioGroup, where the whole group is one stop.

requiredAttributes.description: Required so a sibling Label can reference it with htmlFor. The pairing supplies the accessible name and makes the label text a click target for the box.

requiredAttributes.condition: when legal text, a consequence, or an error message qualifies the choice
requiredAttributes.description: Reference the ids of that text so it is announced with the checkbox instead of being read as unrelated prose.

requiredAttributes.condition: when a required checkbox has failed validation
requiredAttributes.description: Set aria-invalid and reference the error message with aria-describedby so the failure is announced, not just outlined in red.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focusable and in the tab order; focus stays on the control after toggling so the new state is announced in place. The hidden native input is never focused.
accessibility.notes: Radix sets aria-checked="mixed" when checked is "indeterminate", and activating an indeterminate checkbox resolves it to checked — the mixed state is something the parent sets from its children's state, never a third position the user cycles through. Do not convey checked state by color alone; the check mark carries it.

constraints.context: Several independent options where more than one may be selected
constraints.rule: Use a group of Checkboxes

constraints.context: Mutually exclusive options where exactly one may be selected
constraints.rule: Use RadioGroup instead of Checkbox

constraints.context: A setting that applies immediately with no Save step
constraints.rule: Use Switch instead of Checkbox

constraints.context: A parent checkbox summarizing children that are only partly selected
constraints.rule: Set checked to "indeterminate" rather than inventing a third visual state, and make activation resolve to all checked or all unchecked

constraints.context: Any Checkbox
constraints.rule: Give it a visible Label associated by id and htmlFor so the text is clickable and the name is announced

constraints.context: A consent gate that blocks submission
constraints.rule: Set required, and on failure set aria-invalid with the error message referenced by aria-describedby

constraints.context: A checkbox whose value is submitted with a native form
constraints.rule: Set name, and set value when the submitted value is not the default "on"

switch.name: Switch
switch.description: A control that turns a single setting on or off and applies the change immediately, built on Radix UI Switch. Renders a button with role switch and aria-checked plus a hidden native input for form submission, and slides a thumb between two positions to show state.
switch.whenToUse: Use for a setting whose effect is immediate and reversible: enabling notifications, turning on a beta feature, toggling dark mode in a preferences panel. The label names the setting; the switch's position carries on or off.
switch.whenNotToUse: Do not use inside a form that is only committed on Save — a switch implies the change has already happened; use Checkbox. Do not use it to accept terms or capture consent that is submitted with a form; that is a Checkbox. Do not use it to choose among options or for anything that is not a two-state setting; use RadioGroup or Select.

checked.description: Controlled on/off state. Pair it with onCheckedChange; because the change is applied immediately, drive this from the value your backend acknowledged rather than from an unreconciled optimistic guess.

defaultChecked.description: Initial state for an uncontrolled switch.

onCheckedChange.description: Fires with the new boolean state when the user toggles the switch. This is where the setting is persisted — there is no Save step.

values.description: Standard size, suitable for settings rows and forms.
Compact size for dense lists and toolbars. Keep the surrounding row large enough to stay a comfortable touch target.

size.description: Switch size. shadcn adds this on top of the Radix primitive.

disabled.description: Whether the switch is non-interactive. Explain in nearby text why a setting is locked — a disabled switch on its own reads as an unexplained dead control.

required.description: Whether the switch must be on before the form can be submitted. Rarely appropriate: a required toggle usually indicates the choice belongs to a Checkbox in a submitted form.

name.description: Form field name applied to the hidden native input, under which the value is submitted.

value.description: Value submitted when the switch is on.

keyboardInteractions.description: Toggles the switch.
Toggles the switch. This differs from Checkbox, which ignores Enter.
Moves focus to the switch. Each switch is its own tab stop.

requiredAttributes.description: Required so the settings row's Label can reference it with htmlFor, making the label text a click target and the switch's accessible name.

requiredAttributes.condition: when the consequence of the setting is explained in secondary text
requiredAttributes.description: Reference the description's id so the explanation is announced with the control rather than read as loose prose.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focusable and in the tab order; focus stays on the switch after toggling so the new state is announced in place. The hidden native input is never focused.
accessibility.notes: Screen readers announce a switch as on or off rather than checked or unchecked, so the label must name the setting ("Email notifications"), not its state ("On"). Do not add separate On/Off text as the accessible name, and do not rely on the track color alone to communicate state.

constraints.context: A setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped
constraints.rule: Use Switch

constraints.context: A form that is committed with an explicit Save or Submit button
constraints.rule: Use Checkbox instead of Switch

constraints.context: Any Switch
constraints.rule: Give it a visible Label that names the setting, associated by id and htmlFor

constraints.context: The wording of a switch's label
constraints.rule: Name the setting rather than its current state — "Email notifications", never "On"

constraints.context: A toggle whose effect is destructive or hard to reverse, such as disabling two-factor authentication
constraints.rule: Confirm with an AlertDialog before applying the change

constraints.context: A switch backed by a network request
constraints.rule: Reflect the persisted result — revert the position and surface an error if the write fails, rather than leaving an optimistic state that lies about the setting

constraints.context: Choosing among three or more options
constraints.rule: Use RadioGroup or Select instead of a row of Switches

radio-group.name: Radio Group
radio-group.description: A set of mutually exclusive options where exactly one may be selected, built on Radix UI RadioGroup. The group renders role radiogroup and manages a roving tabindex, so the whole group is a single tab stop; each RadioGroupItem is a button with role radio backed by a hidden native input for form submission.
radio-group.whenToUse: Use when the user must pick exactly one option from a small, stable set that is worth seeing all at once: a billing interval, a shipping speed, a visibility level. Showing every option side by side, with its trade-offs visible, is the reason to choose RadioGroup over Select.
radio-group.whenNotToUse: Do not use when more than one option may be selected; use Checkboxes. Do not use for long or runtime-generated lists — past roughly six options the group crowds the form and Select is easier to scan. Do not use for a binary on/off setting; use Switch or a single Checkbox.

value.description: Controlled selected value. Must match the value of exactly one RadioGroupItem in the group.

defaultValue.description: Initially selected value for an uncontrolled group. Omit it when there is no safe default — an unselected group forces a deliberate choice.

onValueChange.description: Fires with the newly selected value. Because selection follows focus, this also fires while the user arrows through the options.

values.description: Options stacked in a column. Up and Down arrows move between them.
Options laid out in a row. Left and Right arrows move between them.

orientation.description: Sets aria-orientation and constrains arrow-key navigation to one axis. Unset by default, which lets both axes navigate; set it to match the visual arrangement whenever the layout is committed to a direction.

disabled.description: Disables every item in the group. To disable one option, set disabled on that RadioGroupItem instead.

required.description: Whether a selection is required before the form can be submitted. Sets aria-required on the group.

name.description: Form field name applied to the items' hidden native inputs, under which the selected value is submitted.

loop.description: Whether arrow-key navigation wraps from the last item back to the first.

values.description: Left-to-right reading order.
Right-to-left reading order, which swaps what Left and Right arrows mean.

dir.description: Reading direction for arrow-key navigation. Inherited from an ambient direction provider when omitted.

subComponents.name: RadioGroupItem
subComponents.description: A single option. Needs a value that is unique within the group and an id so a sibling Label can name it. The selected indicator is rendered internally, so the item takes no children — the option's text goes in a Label next to it, not inside it.

composition.notes: RadioGroupItem must be a descendant of RadioGroup, which supplies the selection context and the roving tabindex; an item outside a group is inert. Each item pairs with a Label whose htmlFor matches the item's id. Wrap the group in a fieldset with a legend so the whole set has an accessible name, and keep the items' order stable — arrow-key navigation follows DOM order.

keyboardInteractions.description: Moves focus into the group, landing on the checked item or, when nothing is checked, on the first enabled one. The group is a single tab stop; Tab again leaves it entirely.
Moves focus to the next item and checks it — selection follows focus.
Moves focus to the previous item and checks it.
Checks the focused item when it is not already checked.
Does nothing. Radix suppresses Enter on radio items to match native radio behavior.

requiredAttributes.condition: on the RadioGroup when its name comes from a visible heading rather than a fieldset legend
requiredAttributes.description: Reference the id of the element that names the whole group. The per-item Labels name individual options; they never name the set.

requiredAttributes.condition: on every RadioGroupItem
requiredAttributes.description: Required so each option's Label can reference it with htmlFor. Without it the option is announced with no name.

requiredAttributes.condition: when a hint or an error message qualifies the whole group
requiredAttributes.description: Put it on the RadioGroup so the guidance is announced once for the set rather than repeated on every option.

requiredAttributes.condition: when a required group has failed validation
requiredAttributes.description: Set it on the RadioGroup so the state is announced for the set. shadcn's item styles also key off aria-invalid, so mirror it onto the RadioGroupItems when the options themselves should show the error.

accessibility.focusManagement: Roving tabindex: exactly one item is tabbable at a time, and arrow keys move focus within the group, checking as they land. Because selection follows focus, a keyboard user cannot browse the options without selecting them — keep the set short and keep onValueChange free of side effects.
accessibility.notes: The group name and the option names are separate obligations: a fieldset legend (or aria-labelledby) names the set, and a Label per item names each option. Do not convey the selected option by color alone; the indicator dot carries it.

constraints.context: Exactly one choice from a small set that should all stay visible
constraints.rule: Use RadioGroup

constraints.context: More than one option may be selected
constraints.rule: Use Checkboxes instead of RadioGroup

constraints.context: More than roughly six options, or a list generated at runtime
constraints.rule: Use Select instead of RadioGroup

constraints.context: Every option in the group
constraints.rule: Give each RadioGroupItem a unique non-empty value and a Label bound by id and htmlFor

constraints.context: The group as a whole
constraints.rule: Give it an accessible group name with a fieldset and legend, or with aria-labelledby

constraints.context: Options arranged in a row
constraints.rule: Set orientation to "horizontal" so aria-orientation and arrow-key navigation match what the user sees

constraints.context: A consequential choice with no obviously safe default
constraints.rule: Leave defaultValue unset rather than pre-selecting an option the user may never consciously confirm

constraints.context: Reacting to a change of selection
constraints.rule: Do not navigate, submit, or trigger destructive side effects on change — selection follows focus, so arrow keys would fire them for every option passed over

select.name: Select
select.description: A select-only combobox built on Radix UI Select: a trigger button that opens a portalled listbox of options. The trigger renders role combobox, the content renders role listbox, and each item renders role option, while a hidden native select carries the value into form submission. It is not a native select element — the list is fully stylable but always renders in a layer above the page, and it accepts no typed input.
select.whenToUse: Use to pick one value from a known list that is too long to show inline: a country, a timezone, a project, a status. It earns its click from roughly six options upward, where a RadioGroup would crowd the form.
select.whenNotToUse: Do not use for two to five options that fit on screen — a RadioGroup shows them all without a click. Do not use when more than one value may be chosen; Select is single-value, so use checkboxes or a dedicated multi-select. Do not use when the user needs to type to filter a long list or to enter a value that is not in it; use a combobox. When the platform's native picker is what you actually want, on dense mobile forms, use a native select instead.

value.description: Controlled selected value; must match the value of one SelectItem. The empty string means nothing is selected and shows the SelectValue placeholder.
